title: Data-Center Market Is Booming Amid Shift to Cloud
summary: The data-center market is experiencing a boom driven by the shift to cloud computing, even as many businesses are moving IT operations online. This has led to increased demand and consolidation among data-center operators as co-location service providers acquire facilities to lease space to major cloud services like Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The sector is seeing more deals as data-center landlords and cloud providers seek more facilities.

title: BD: Medication Management Platform
summary: BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) has launched a new software application designed to help hospitals and health systems identify drug diversion, a major driver of the opioid crisis within healthcare settings. This application, part of the BD HealthSight™ platform, leverages data from existing BD products and Electronic Medical Records to provide actionable insights for diversion investigations. It utilizes machine learning algorithms, developed in partnership with Microsoft, to detect risky behaviors and automate the review process, enhancing patient and staff safety.

title: CISOs moving budgets from staffing to new tools: Nikhil Taneja, Radware
summary: Nikhil Taneja of Radware discusses how CISOs are shifting budgets from staffing to new tools like machine learning and automation to combat evolving cybersecurity threats. The article highlights the changing threat landscape, the challenges of cloud security, and the increasing importance of robust solutions to prevent attacks like DDoS and insider threats. Radware's role in providing high-availability and real-time deep learning security solutions is also detailed.

title: Microsoft and Kroger want to show you Minority Report-style ads
summary: Microsoft and Kroger are partnering to develop high-tech grocery stores that will feature digital shelving displays with real-time pricing and personalized advertisements, reminiscent of "Minority Report." These ads will be tailored to individual customers based on demographics and, for opted-in users, previous purchase history, utilizing facial recognition and AI. While not cashierless like Amazon Go, the stores aim to enhance the shopping experience with guided navigation and in-app scanning for faster checkout.

title: Microsoft Stock Could Enter Bear Market
summary: Microsoft stock, despite outperforming in 2018, showed signs of deterioration in late 2018, breaking key technical support levels. This analysis suggests that its bull market run might be ending, with potential for a deep correction and a bear market in 2019. The article highlights potential downside targets and crucial support levels the stock needs to hold to prevent further declines.

title: Microsoft to explore investment opportunities in Pakistan: Bill Gates
summary: Billionaire Bill Gates has indicated that Microsoft Corporation is open to exploring investment opportunities in Pakistan. This desire was conveyed in a letter from Gates to Prime Minister Imran Khan, delivered during a meeting where the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation also reaffirmed its commitment to polio eradication and healthcare improvement in the country. The prime minister welcomed the support and reiterated Pakistan's dedication to eradicating polio and implementing a transformative social and economic agenda.

title: First Microsoft Teams Phones are Generally Available from Yealink. AudioCodes, Crestron and Polycom coming soon
summary: Yealink phones are the first IP Phones for Microsoft Teams to be generally available, with Crestron also having a GA model and more devices from AudioCodes, Crestron, and Polycom expected soon. The article details the user experience for Teams phones, including sign-in options, calling features, meeting capabilities, and voicemail access for both personal and shared modes. It also provides links to Microsoft's documentation on Teams phones and their deployment.

title: CES 2019: The rise of AI in automotive
summary: This article discusses the prominent role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) at CES 2019, particularly within the automotive industry. It highlights Microsoft's vision for connected and safe mobility experiences, showcasing partnerships with companies like LG Electronics, Visteon, ZF, and Elektrobit that are leveraging Azure IoT, AI, and mixed reality for autonomous driving and in-car intelligence. The article also projects significant growth in AI revenue for the automotive sector and emphasizes the transformative potential of AI in shaping the future of vehicles.

title: Oil industry makes landmark investment in CO2 air capture
summary: Chevron Corp. and Occidental Petroleum Corp. have made a landmark investment in Carbon Engineering, a company deploying technology to capture carbon dioxide directly from the air. This significant collaboration marks the first major public equity investment by oil companies in a direct air capture firm, aiming to accelerate the technology's commercialization and deployment. The move comes as direct air capture gains traction, with new federal tax credits and increasing recognition of its potential role in addressing climate change, despite some environmental criticisms regarding its cost-effectiveness compared to other carbon capture methods.

title: Walgreens Boots Alliance and Microsoft establish strategic partnership to transform health care delivery
summary: Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) and Microsoft Corp. have formed a strategic partnership to revolutionize healthcare delivery through new models, technology, and retail innovations. This collaboration will leverage Microsoft Azure and AI with WBA's extensive reach and healthcare services to create more personalized, affordable, and accessible healthcare globally. The partnership includes a multiyear R&D investment, the pilot of "digital health corners" in WBA stores, and the migration of WBA’s IT infrastructure to Microsoft Azure.

title: NVIDIA Resets The Self-Driving Bar Again With AutoPilot Supporting 'Level 2+'
summary: NVIDIA announced its DRIVE AutoPilot system at CES 2019, which it describes as the "world's first commercially available Level 2+ automated driving system" that will enable supervised self-driving vehicles by 2020. The company also revealed that Mercedes-Benz has chosen NVIDIA as its AI partner for developing next-generation vehicles. Additionally, NVIDIA launched the new GeForce RTX 2060 GPU and announced over 40 new gaming laptops featuring GeForce RTX GPUs.

title: Kroger teams with Microsoft on high-tech Cincinnati test store: PHOTOS (Video)
summary: Kroger Co. has partnered with Microsoft Corp. to develop and test new in-store digital technologies, including digital shelf displays, at a Greater Cincinnati store. This collaboration aims to enhance the shopping experience through advanced tech applications. The article features photos and video related to these scanning devices and digital integrations.

title: Yealink, Crestron release first Microsoft Teams phones
summary: Yealink and Crestron have received certification for the first Microsoft Teams phones, addressing a previous lack of hardware support for the cloud-based collaboration app. This development makes Microsoft Teams a more credible PBX story, especially for enterprises migrating from Skype for Business. While other vendors like Polycom and AudioCodes are expected to follow, Teams users still have fewer certified phone options compared to Skype for Business.

title: NRF Big Show Report: Kroger, Starbucks and the journey to intelligent retail
summary: The article discusses how Starbucks and Kroger are adopting intelligent retail operations, driven by a shared customer-centric philosophy and partnerships with Microsoft. Both companies are leveraging technology like AI, IoT, and cloud platforms to enhance customer experience, improve operational efficiency, and innovate in their respective segments. The report highlights their strategies and insights shared at the National Retail Federation (NRF) Big Show.

title: First battery-free Bluetooth sticker sensor tag demonstrated
summary: Wiliot, a semiconductor innovator, has demonstrated the first-ever sticker-sized, battery-free Bluetooth sensor tag powered by scavenging ambient radio frequencies. This technology allows for low-cost, disposable electronics capable of connecting products with packaging, enabling new IoT applications. AWS, Samsung, and Avery Dennison have invested in Wiliot, recognizing the potential of these tags for real-time tracking, interactive consumer engagement, and automated product management.

title: The Ultimate Digital Transformation: Microsoft Helps Kroger Become Tech Company
summary: Kroger, America's largest grocery retailer, is undergoing a significant digital transformation by partnering with Microsoft to become a technology company. They are developing and selling cloud-based "Retail as a Service" (RaaS) solutions, powered by Microsoft Azure and IoT, to other retailers. This initiative aims to redefine the shopping experience through innovations like paperless smart shelves and hyper-personalization, creating new revenue opportunities beyond traditional grocery operations.

title: Zero Latency partners with Microsoft, HP and Intel for next-gen free-roam VR
summary: Zero Latency, a pioneer in free-roam multiplayer virtual reality (VR) entertainment, has partnered with Microsoft, HP, and Intel to develop its next-generation VR platform. This collaboration involves the provision of software, hardware, and marketing assistance to enhance Zero Latency's global reach. The initiative aims to expand VR experiences through location-based entertainment, leveraging technology such as mixed reality headsets, cloud services, and Intel NUC VR platforms.

title: Google Cloud Acquisition Targets: ServiceNow, Atlassian, Splunk? Pure Speculation
summary: This article speculates on potential acquisition targets for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to help it close the revenue gap with AWS and Azure, specifically mentioning ServiceNow, Atlassian, Splunk, and Zayo. It analyzes the pros and cons of each potential deal, highlighting challenges related to market capitalization, sales models, and integration for each company. The author concludes that while Wall Street speculates, there are no credible reports of actual takeover discussions.

title: Tencent Music Co-Presidents Cross Into Billionaire Terrain
summary: Two co-presidents of Tencent Music Entertainment Group briefly became billionaires following gains in the company's shares after its New York Stock Exchange IPO in December 2018. While Xie Zhenyu's fortune was just under $1 billion and Xie Guomin's fell back, the company's valuation and user base are significant. They still have considerable ground to cover to match Tencent Holdings Chairman Pony Ma's wealth.

title: REIT Warehouse Logistics Being Redefined by Prologis
summary: Prologis, a leading logistics REIT, is redefining warehouse logistics by developing multi-story distribution centers in urban areas to meet the rising demand for faster e-commerce delivery. Their "Georgetown Crossroads" project in Seattle, the first U.S. multi-story warehouse serviceable by tractor-trailer trucks, highlights a strategy to densify sites in land-constrained metropolitan areas. This approach addresses the need to be closer to consumers and overcomes the limitations of traditional single-story warehouses on city outskirts, though it involves higher land acquisition and construction costs.

title: Caterpillar, Nvidia Warnings Send Wall Street Tumbling
summary: U.S. stocks tumbled following warnings from Caterpillar and Nvidia, which highlighted concerns about a slowing Chinese economy and the impact of tariffs on corporate profits. Caterpillar missed profit estimates due to softening demand in China and rising costs, while Nvidia cut its revenue forecast due to weak demand and lower data center sales. This sent major indexes like the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite lower, despite overall positive earnings reports.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics
summary: This article reviews the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics (DMSA), highlighting key changes since the previous report. It discusses shifts in vendor positions, new entrants, and removals, focusing on the evolution of major players like Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, SAP, Teradata, IBM, Snowflake, Google, and MarkLogic. The article also touches upon the general trends in DMSA, emphasizing the growing importance of cloud and the diverse approaches taken by niche and leading providers.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Science and Machine Learning Platforms
summary: This article reviews the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Science and Machine Learning Platforms, highlighting changes in vendor positioning and evaluation criteria. It discusses new additions to the report, vendor movements within the quadrants (Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, Niche Players), and key strengths of prominent providers like RapidMiner, TIBCO Software, SAS, Alteryx, Dataiku, MathWorks, H2O.AI, Databricks, and Domino. The piece emphasizes Gartner's advice for buyers to consider specific tools based on their needs rather than solely on quadrant placement.

title: Why Advanced Micro Devices might be important for service providers
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is becoming increasingly important for service providers due to its high-performance server processors like Epyc, which are crucial for hyperscale cloud players and data center updates. The company reported strong financial results in 2018, with significant growth in its data center business, and expects further adoption with its upcoming "Rome" processor, which offers improved performance and socket compatibility. As operators like AT&T, Sprint, and Comcast transform their networks with generic hardware, AMD's server technology is poised to play a key role in their data center evolution.

title: Kroger latest company to consolidate CIO and CDO roles
summary: Grocery chain Kroger is consolidating its Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Chief Digital Officer (CDO) roles, with current CDO Yael Cosset taking over as CIO from the retiring Christopher Hjelm. This move reflects a broader trend of aligning digital and technology initiatives within companies and underscores Kroger's aggressive pursuit of technology, including its partnership with Microsoft. The consolidation aims to further integrate digital projects into the company's core functions and enhance omnichannel customer experiences.

title: Intel names permanent CEO, said to benefit firm’s Israel operations
summary: Intel has named Robert Swan as its permanent CEO. This appointment is expected to benefit the firm's operations in Israel due to Swan's familiarity with its activities there. Intel has significant investments and operations in Israel, including manufacturing and R&D centers, and recently announced an $11 billion investment for a new plant in Kiryat Gat.

title: Intel's new CEO is facing the same old challenges
summary: Robert "Bob" Swan has been appointed as Intel's CEO at a critical time, inheriting significant challenges in manufacturing, innovation, and navigating a potentially declining PC market and slowing data center growth. Despite strong financial results in 2018, Intel faces intense competition from rivals like Samsung, TSMC, AMD, and ARM licensees, alongside the technical hurdle of pushing past the limits of Moore's Law. Swan, with a finance background, will need to demonstrate his ability to adapt Intel's strategy to these evolving industry dynamics.

title: Hershey emphasizes savings from multiyear ERP transformation
summary: The Hershey Company is undergoing a multiyear ERP transformation, implementing new modules for trade promotion and marketing expenses, which CEO Michele Buck calls a "key enabler" for digital transformation. While capital expenditures are projected to be $330 million to $350 million, CFO Patricia Little expects significant savings, with part flowing into 2020. The company is partnering with Accenture and SAP for an S/4HANA implementation to streamline operations and enhance analytics, anticipating margin for growth program savings between $150 million and $175 million.

title: Johnson Controls launches high-end smart thermostat
summary: Johnson Controls has launched GLAS, a high-end smart thermostat priced at $319, continuing its long history in thermostat innovation. This premium device uses Windows 10 IoT Core, Microsoft Azure, and Qualcomm Snapdragon 410E, and includes advanced sensors for indoor and outdoor air quality, along with voice assistant integration. The company emphasizes the product's advanced technology, connectivity with smart home systems, and sleek design as key differentiators in the crowded smart thermostat market.

title: New Accenture Microsoft Business Group will empower enterprises to thrive in the era of digital disruption
summary: Accenture and Microsoft, along with their joint venture Avanade, have launched the Accenture Microsoft Business Group to expand service capabilities and joint solution development. This new group, comprising over 45,000 professionals, aims to help clients overcome disruption and lead digital transformation by leveraging Microsoft cloud technologies. It will focus on migrating clients to Azure, optimizing business processes with Dynamics 365, and fostering collaboration with Microsoft 365.

title: After 5 years, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has transformed more than the stock price
summary: This article reflects on Satya Nadella's five-year tenure as Microsoft CEO, highlighting his success in not only boosting the stock price but more importantly, transforming the company's culture. Nadella shifted Microsoft from a monolithic, Windows-centric approach to one focused on services, cloud, cross-platform cooperation, and customer needs, including strategic acquisitions like LinkedIn and GitHub. The piece credits him with successfully navigating broad cultural changes within the large organization.

title: Google selects Equinix for submarine cable landing station in LA
summary: Google has chosen Equinix's LA4 data center as the landing point for its upcoming Curie submarine cable, which will connect the US with Chile. This marks the first direct submarine link between the two countries in 20 years. The cable, named after Marie Skłodowska Curie, will stretch over 10,000 km and aims to meet the increasing demand for high-capacity, low-latency global connectivity.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms
summary: This article analyzes Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms, highlighting the increasing importance of augmented analytics, automation, and natural language processing. It discusses key changes in vendor positioning, with Microsoft solidifying its lead and ThoughtSpot emerging as a market leader, while also reviewing the performance of other significant players like Tableau, Qlik, MicroStrategy, TIBCO Software, Sisense, and Looker.

title: Form 8-K GARTNER INC For: Feb 14
summary: This article reports on Gartner Inc.'s 8-K filing from February 14, 2019, detailing investor presentations made on that date, including slides filed as Exhibit 99.1. The filing emphasizes Gartner's business model, strategy for long-term growth, and financial outlook, highlighting its "Gartner Formula" for sustained double-digit growth across its segments like Global Technology Sales (GTS) and Global Business Sales (GBS). It also provides details on the company's organizational structure, leadership, and financial objectives.

title: India a $50 billion market for energy storage: AES
summary: India presents a potential investment opportunity of $50 billion in battery storage facilities, according to Andres Gluski, CEO of AES Corp, driven by its ambitious renewable energy targets and electric mobility push. The country's first 10 MW battery-storage system, built by AES and Mitsubishi Corp. for almost $9 million, was launched in New Delhi to support the grid. Energy storage is seen as crucial for integrating variable renewable energy, optimizing transmission and distribution investments, and addressing grid challenges.

title: A Few Minutes With PTC's Jim Heppelmann
summary: This article features an interview with Jim Heppelmann, CEO of PTC, discussing the company's focus on integrating AR and IoT technologies into enterprise solutions. Heppelmann details PTC's strategy for industrial AR through its Vuforia suite, highlighting acquisitions and significant R&D investments that have led to substantial growth. The article emphasizes PTC's efforts to make AR accessible for various industrial applications and its impact on productivity for front-line workers.

title: FatPipe Announces SD-WAN for Azure to Address Connectivity Issues for Cloud-Based Real-Time Applications
summary: FatPipe Networks announced the general availability of its SD-WAN for Azure solution through the Microsoft Azure Marketplace. This new offering aims to resolve connectivity and performance issues for cloud-based real-time applications like Office 365, particularly benefiting large user groups and enhancing applications such as Azure Stream Analytics by ensuring session continuity with patented MPSec technology, WAN optimization, and QoS.

title: Cybersecurity Brothers Join Billionaire Club
summary: Ken and Michael Xie, founders of the cybersecurity firm Fortinet Inc., have become billionaires due to their company's success in the growing cybersecurity market. Fortinet, valued at $13 billion, has surpassed market growth rates and its shares have significantly increased since its 2009 IPO. Ken Xie, the largest individual shareholder, and Michael Xie continue to lead the company, focusing on emerging trends like mobile security.

title: Nokia Bets it All on 5G
summary: Nokia is embarking on a bold strategy to bet its future on 5G technology, repositioning itself after divesting its mobile handset business and undergoing significant acquisitions. Despite a challenging competitive landscape and internal reorganization, CEO Rajeev Suri expresses confidence in 5G's potential to drive growth, especially in the enterprise market, anticipating a stronger performance in the latter half of 2019 and 2020. The article highlights Nokia's history of reinvention and the risks and opportunities associated with its current 5G-centric gambit amidst geopolitical headwinds and the evolving tech industry.

title: Machine learning is the biggest disruptive tech: AMD CTO Mark Papermaster
summary: AMD CTO Mark Papermaster discusses the significance of the company's new 7nm chips in meeting the insatiable demand for computational power, especially in data centers and mobile devices. He highlights machine learning as the biggest disruptive technology, noting its potential to leverage data and predict results, while also addressing concerns about AI and robotics replacing human jobs. Papermaster also touches on GPU usage in the crypto space, indicating AMD's focus on broader GPU markets in gaming, servers, and blockchain.

title: Kemp 360 Vision analyzes F5, Nginx data
summary: Kemp Technologies has updated its 360 Vision predictive analytics service to include data from F5 Networks and Nginx load balancers, allowing for multivendor ADC ecosystem management. This SaaS application identifies potential problems and suggests remediation steps, with upcoming support for KVM, AWS, and Microsoft Azure. The update also adds automated load balancer deployment to Kemp 360 Central.

title: Xiaomi-backed Up Fintech plans US$150 million IPO in New York
summary: Up Fintech Holding, an online broker serving Chinese investors and backed by Xiaomi, is planning to raise US$150 million in an initial public offering on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The company, which operates as Tiger Trade App, nearly doubled its revenue last year to US$33.6 million but reported a net loss of US$44.3 million. Up Fintech claims to be the largest online broker for global Chinese investors in US securities trading volume, with a 58.4% market share in 2017.

title: Microsoft and Trimble made a hard hat with HoloLens built-in
summary: Microsoft partnered with Trimble to create the XR10, a hard hat with a built-in HoloLens 2, aimed at bringing mixed reality technology to construction sites. This collaboration showcases Microsoft's strategy to expand the practical application of its HoloLens device beyond office environments. Pricing for the XR10 is yet to be announced but it will be available concurrently with the standard HoloLens 2.

title: Cyber Security Market to cross USD 300 billion by 2024
summary: The global Cyber Security Market is projected to exceed $300 billion by 2024, growing from over $120 billion, driven by the increasing need to mitigate security risks as enterprises adopt cloud platforms and mobile devices. Organizations reported a significant rise in cybersecurity spending and an increase in cyber-attacks on mobile devices, fueling demand for security solutions. The market will see strong growth across various sectors including large enterprises, SMEs, transportation, and IT & telecom, with specific growth predicted for IAAM and infrastructure protection segments.

title: Philips showcases augmented reality for image-guided therapies
summary: Royal Philips has unveiled a new mixed reality concept for minimally invasive surgeries, developed with Microsoft, at MWC 2019 in Barcelona. This concept utilizes the Philips Azurion image-guided therapy platform and Microsoft’s HoloLens 2 to create a 3D holographic augmented reality environment for surgeons. The aim is to integrate live imaging and vital data, controlled by voice and gestures, to enhance precision in therapy and improve patient outcomes.

title: Microsoft boosts HoloLens performance, seeking corporate users
summary: Microsoft is launching an improved version of its HoloLens augmented reality goggles, the HoloLens 2, aimed at corporate users, with a lower price point and enhanced features. The company is positioning the device as a tool for various industries, including healthcare and manufacturing, and is also offering it via a monthly subscription. This move reflects Microsoft's strategy to democratize AI and mixed reality technology and generate revenue beyond device sales through cloud software.

title: Trimble’s XR10 puts HoloLens 2 in a hard hat for construction, oil & gas, more
summary: Trimble has introduced the XR10 device, which integrates Microsoft's new HoloLens 2 into a hard hat, making mixed reality accessible for workers in safety-controlled environments like construction, oil, and gas. This solution, developed through Microsoft's HoloLens Customization Program, allows users to review design models, view complex instructions, and collaborate remotely. It also highlights Trimble's ongoing commitment to advancing mixed-reality technology in enterprise applications.

title: Forbes' billionaires list includes 20 from Michigan
summary: Forbes' annual list of the world's richest people includes 20 individuals with ties to Michigan, ten of whom currently reside in the state. The article highlights each Michigan-connected billionaire, detailing their net worth, global ranking, and their connection to the Great Lakes State. Notable figures include Larry Page, Steve Ballmer, and various business leaders from prominent Michigan companies like Meijer, Quicken Loans, and Stryker Corp.

title: Robots Built This Futuristic House That Generates More Energy Than it Needs
summary: The DFAB House in Dübendorf, Switzerland, is the world's first home designed, planned, and built primarily with digital processes and robots, generating 1.5 times more energy than it needs through rooftop photovoltaics. Developed by ETH Zurich, it showcases pioneering construction technologies like Mesh Mould, Smart Slab, and Spatial Timber Assemblies. This experimental building serves as a living research area, integrating smart home technologies and demonstrating a futuristic approach to sustainable architecture.

title: C.H. Robinson CEO John Wiehoff Takes Work And Play Seriously
summary: John Wiehoff, CEO of C.H. Robinson, believes a "work hard, play hard" mentality is crucial for both personal success and building a strong company culture. During his 17-year tenure as CEO, C.H. Robinson's stock price increased nearly sixfold and revenue grew significantly, a testament to his leadership and focus on long-term vision and a sustainable culture. Wiehoff, who is retiring from his CEO role, emphasizes integrity, leadership, and a commitment to employees, customers, and a broad network of mentors.

title: Preparing for a world of change: Microsoft’s forward-looking approach to transfer pricing execution and monitoring
summary: This article details how PwC collaborated with Microsoft to overhaul its transfer pricing execution and monitoring processes. Facing complex regulatory environments and business model transformations, Microsoft automated intercompany processes within the SAP platform, established a new Operational Transfer Pricing Team, and integrated PwC's pre-built programs to improve efficiency, reduce risks, and achieve significant benefits in cycle time and audit preparedness.

title: Nvidia to make largest acquisition in its history with $6.9 billion deal for Mellanox
F5 Networks paying $670M to acquire NGINX, a web server that runs a big chunk of the internet
summary: F5 Networks is acquiring NGINX, a popular web server, for $670 million. This acquisition aims to transition F5 from a hardware company to one focused on software and services for application infrastructure, bridging app development and security across various cloud environments. NGINX will retain its brand and open-source strategy, with its leadership joining F5.

title: US gaming firm Nvidia to buy Israeli chip maker Mellanox for $6.9 billion
summary: US gaming and computer graphics giant Nvidia Corp. is set to acquire Israeli chip maker Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion in cash. This deal marks the second-largest tech acquisition in Israel's history and will enhance Nvidia's capabilities in high-speed data center solutions. Mellanox, founded in 1999, specializes in servers and storage switching solutions and has seen significant demand for its products.

title: F5 Networks Acquires NGINX For $670 Million
summary: F5 Networks has acquired NGINX, a popular open-source web server company, for approximately $670 million. This acquisition aims to strengthen F5's growth trajectory by accelerating its software and multi-cloud transformation, bridging NetOps and DevOps with consistent application services. NGINX will maintain its brand and leadership, leveraging F5's global sales and channel infrastructure.

title: From Bentonville to Seoul, Jay Jorgensen Becomes General Counsel of South Korea's Coupang
summary: Jay Jorgensen, former executive vice president and global chief ethics and compliance officer of Walmart Inc., has been appointed as the new general counsel for Coupang, South Korea's largest and fastest-growing e-commerce company. This move brings Jorgensen's extensive experience in retail and compliance, including building a world-class program at Walmart, to the rapidly expanding South Korean e-commerce giant. Coupang, often referred to as the "Amazon of South Korea," is reportedly eyeing an initial public stock offering in 2019 or 2020.

title: Microsoft Sets Date To End The support For Windows 7
summary: Microsoft announced that it will end support for Windows 7 and Office 2010 on January 14, 2020, meaning no more software or security updates. Despite Windows 10 surpassing it in market share recently, Windows 7 still holds a significant portion of the desktop OS market, making the transition a challenge for Microsoft. The company plans to notify users to encourage upgrades to Windows 10 or purchase a new PC.

title: Your U.S. Equity Fund Is More Global Than You Think
summary: This article examines how U.S. equity funds are more globally exposed than commonly perceived by analyzing revenue streams by region. Morningstar's new proprietary data reveals that many popular U.S. index-tracking ETFs have significant revenue exposure outside the United States, particularly in emerging Asian markets and the eurozone. The analysis highlights that relying on a company's headquarters or stock listing alone provides a flawed picture of a fund's true geographic allocation.

title: Why Now Might Be a Good Time to Buy QQQ
summary: This article discusses reasons why the Invesco QQQ ETF could be a good investment. It highlights QQQ's focus on large-cap growth, particularly in technology and related sectors, its strong historical performance relative to the S&P 500, and its high liquidity. The article also touches on potential risks like sector concentration and higher volatility compared to broader market indices.

title: Microsoft Teams Direct Routing Media Bypass Now Available
summary: Microsoft Teams Direct Routing Media Bypass is now available, allowing media to flow directly between the end user and the Session Border Controller (SBC) instead of routing through the Microsoft Phone System, which can optimize network performance. The article explains how media bypass works, its benefits, certified SBCs, and considerations regarding codecs and transcoding. It also notes that Skype for Business 3PIP phones do not support media bypass, while Microsoft Teams phones will.

title: Developers Lean on Joint Ventures to Fund Hyperscale Data Centers
summary: Data center developers are increasingly using joint ventures to fund the construction of hyperscale data centers due to the enormous capital requirements of such projects. This strategy allows even large publicly traded developers like Digital Realty Trust and QTS Realty to partner with institutional investors, who are eager to invest in data centers leased to investment-grade cloud providers. Joint ventures provide a mechanism for developers to access significant capital, monetize existing assets, and reduce reliance on equity markets to fund future growth.

title: How Salesforce paved the way for the SaaS platform approach
summary: This article details how Salesforce pioneered the SaaS platform approach, starting from simple customization requests in its early CRM product to the development of APIs, the AppExchange, and eventually Force.com (now Salesforce Lightning Platform). It highlights the company's incremental steps in building an ecosystem where other companies could build applications on its infrastructure, effectively setting a new standard for enterprise SaaS.

title: S-1
summary: This S-1 filing by Zoom Video Communications, Inc. details its initial public offering of Class A common stock, outlining the company's business model, competitive strengths, market opportunity, and financial performance. The company highlights its video-first communications platform, rapid revenue growth, and positive operational cash flow, while also disclosing risk factors and the dual-class stock structure concentrating voting control with pre-IPO stockholders.

title: iShares U.S. Equity Factor Rotation Active ETF
summary: This article provides a comprehensive profile of the iShares U.S. Equity Factor Rotation Active ETF (DYNF), detailing its price, category, inception date, expense ratio, and AUM. It also includes sections on its top holdings, concentration analysis, valuation, dividend information, performance metrics, and ESG scores. The report offers an in-depth look at this active ETF's characteristics and comparisons to its peers.

title: 'Apex Legends' boosts Electronic Arts
summary: Electronic Arts Inc. is seeing a significant boost due to the success of its new free-to-play game, "Apex Legends," which generated $92 million in its first month and is poised for further growth with the introduction of battle passes. This resurgence coincides with a general increase in digital game spending worldwide, driving up stock prices for EA and other major video game publishers. However, Epic Games' "Fortnite" has also gained a substantial number of new users, matching "Apex Legends'" user base since its release.

title: Introducing AutoCAD 2020: See What’s New
summary: Autodesk has released AutoCAD 2020, featuring a new dark theme, significant performance improvements, and enhanced tools like Quick Measure and the Blocks palette. The update also includes a redesigned Purge feature, improved DWG Compare, and new partnerships with Microsoft OneDrive and Box for streamlined cloud workflows. These innovations are also available in AutoCAD LT 2020.

title: Mayor Turner Establishes Complete Communities Improvement Fund to Accelerate Initiative’s Progress
summary: Mayor Sylvester Turner has established the Complete Communities Improvement Fund with an initial fundraising goal of $25 million to accelerate his Complete Communities initiative. The fund, which already has $10 million in contributions, aims to leverage public and private funds for neighborhood improvements in under-resourced areas based on resident-developed action plans. Key initiatives include increasing mixed-income housing, providing micro-lending and down-payment assistance, job skills training, scholarships, and economic development.

title: Goodyear empowers its global workforce with Microsoft 365’s intelligent tools
summary: Goodyear is leveraging Microsoft 365 to empower its global workforce and drive innovation. The company's 64,000 associates in over 150 countries use Microsoft 365's intelligent tools for collaborative, agile, and efficient work in a secure digital environment. This strategy helps Goodyear connect with customers and deliver innovative products and services worldwide.

title: Sally Beauty launches mobile-first site, adds Apple Pay, Instagram shopping
summary: Sally Beauty Holdings Inc. has launched a redesigned mobile-first website, integrated Apple Pay as a payment option, and is developing a mobile app. These initiatives are part of the company's strategy to transform its retail business for the e-commerce world, including offering a shop-by-solution experience and enabling direct purchases through Instagram.

title: iShares U.S. Equity Factor Rotation Active ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:DYNF)
summary: The iShares U.S. Equity Factor Rotation Active ETF (DYNF) is an actively managed ETF that invests in large- and mid-cap U.S. stocks based on five equity style factors. Launched on March 19, 2019, and managed by BlackRock, the fund currently has $35.74 billion in market capitalization and $36.47 billion in assets under management. Its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft.

title: NVIDIA Is A Data Center Company Now
summary: NVIDIA's acquisition of Mellanox for $6.9 billion signifies its strategic shift from primarily a GPU company to a full-fledged data center company. This move leverages NVIDIA's success in High-Performance Compute (HPC) and AI with GPUs, integrating Mellanox's data center networking expertise to address the growing demands of data science and hyperscale workloads. The article highlights how NVIDIA is expanding its ecosystem to support diverse data center needs, from specialized accelerators to broader infrastructure solutions.

title: This Indian Tech Billionaire Just Gave the Biggest Ever Donation to Charity
summary: India's second-richest man, Azim Premji, made history by donating $7.5 billion to his Azim Premji Foundation, marking the largest single contribution to an Indian foundation and potentially the biggest individual donation to charity ever. The donation supports rural education and the development of universities. Premji has now donated a total of $21 billion to charity, aligning with the Giving Pledge initiative.

title: Global X S&P 500 Catholic Values ETF (CATH) Holdings
summary: This article provides detailed holdings and sector weightings for the Global X S&P 500 Catholic Values ETF (CATH) as of August 11, with NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft being its top holdings. The ETF invests in S&P 500 companies screened to align with Catholic values, holding 99.93% in stocks with a net asset value of $1.3 billion. It also lists key financial metrics and related ETFs.

title: Vitamin Supplement Manufacturer Automates HR Processes with Ease
summary: International Vitamin Corporation (IVC) HRIS & Compensation Manager, Macie Benjelloun, successfully modernized the company's HR processes by implementing ADP Marketplace solutions. By integrating existing HR systems like iCIMS and SAP Concur with ADP Workforce Now, IVC achieved significant data automation, streamlined hiring, and saved an estimated $60,000 annually. This digital transformation allowed the HR team to shift focus from transactional tasks to strategic business partnering.

title: Greg Moore joins Microsoft Healthcare to lead emerging technology and alliances
summary: Dr. Gregory Moore has joined Microsoft Healthcare as Corporate Vice President, Health Technology and Alliances, to lead emerging technology and alliances. He will focus on fostering dedicated research and development collaborations with strategic partners, integrating AI and machine learning solutions to enable personalized care, and advocating for an open, interoperable, and AI-infused foundation for healthcare delivery. His appointment underscores Microsoft's commitment to leveraging cloud, AI, and research capabilities to improve health insights, experiences, and outcomes.

title: The Corporate Entrepreneur: Matthew Mottola at Microsoft
summary: Matthew Mottola, MS'17, began his entrepreneurial journey by freelancing in college, which led him to Babson's MSEL program to build a platform connecting student freelancers to businesses. Despite initial setbacks and a pivot to Gigster, Mottola eventually brought his vision for integrating freelance talent into corporate structures to Microsoft, spearheading the Microsoft 365 Freelance Toolkit. His story highlights leveraging entrepreneurial skills within a large organization to solve a systemic problem.

title: Microsoft staff email chain prompts sexual harassment investigations
summary: Microsoft's executive leadership team is investigating allegations of sexual harassment and discrimination that emerged from a 90-page employee email chain. The company's chief people officer has acknowledged the allegations and plans to create forums for feedback. This incident follows a previous gender discrimination lawsuit against Microsoft and highlights ongoing challenges within the tech industry regarding workplace misconduct.

title: Qualcomm aims to take on Nvidia, Intel with new AI chips
summary: Qualcomm is entering the artificial intelligence chip market with its new Cloud AI 100 chip, aiming to compete with Nvidia and Intel. The company plans to target smaller, simpler data centers with power-efficient chips designed for "inference" tasks, leveraging its expertise from mobile phone chip development. Testing with partners like Microsoft is expected to begin later this year, with mass production in 2020.

title: Colleges and universities team up with Microsoft to address the technical skills gap by building global talent pipelines for AI, data science, computer science and cybersecurity
summary: Microsoft Corp. announced new partnerships with global higher education institutions to integrate its technical skills programs and credentials. These collaborations aim to address the growing 21st-century talent gap in fields like AI, computer science, cybersecurity, and data science by preparing students for future jobs. Institutions like Bellevue College, Purdue University Global, and University of London are incorporating Microsoft courses, allowing students to earn industry credentials and college credits simultaneously.

title: SoFi Select 500 ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the SoFi Select 500 ETF (SFY), which was created on April 11, 2019, by SoFi. The ETF primarily invests in large-cap US equities selected by market capitalization, currently holding $653.65 million in assets under management across 501 holdings. Key holdings include major technology companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon, and Apple, alongside recent changes in share counts for various stocks.

title: Del Monte Foods makes SAP ERP migration to AWS
summary: Del Monte Foods migrated its SAP ERP system to Amazon Web Services (AWS) to consolidate IT systems, reduce costs, and gain flexibility. This move, driven by prior acquisition challenges, allowed them to cut IT costs by about 35% without disrupting business processes. Analysts noted Del Monte is ahead of the curve in fully moving core ERP to the cloud, as many companies remain on-premises or in vendor-hosted environments.

title: Red Dead Redemption 2 Is a Key Revenue Growth Driver for Take-Two
summary: Take-Two Interactive is heavily reliant on popular franchises like Red Dead Redemption 2 to drive revenue growth, similar to how Grand Theft Auto boosted sales in 2014. Red Dead Redemption 2 achieved the biggest opening in entertainment history with over $725 million in sales in its first three days and sold over 23 million units within four months, making it the best-selling video game of 2018 in the US. The game's success has significantly contributed to Take-Two's financial performance and unit sales.

title: Cloud Computing: The Digital Infrastructure Powering Today's Businesses
summary: This article discusses how cloud computing has fundamentally transformed business IT, moving from on-premise infrastructure to remote, scalable services. It highlights the financial advantages, ease of management, flexibility, platform power, interoperability, and enablement of emerging technologies as key drivers of its growth. The article concludes that while cloud adoption is still relatively early, it is becoming a foundational tool for businesses of all sizes, with increasing spending and widespread implementation expected.

title: Microsoft buys up more metro-Phoenix land for $37 million
summary: Microsoft has purchased an additional 147 acres of land in Goodyear, Arizona, for $37 million, marking its second significant land acquisition in the metro Phoenix area. This new plot is located near Loop 303, and a development agreement might be presented to the City Council as early as May. The company's previous purchase in 2018 involved 279 acres for $48 million, intended for a "five-building technology center" that is projected to use a large amount of water.

title: Wipro breach highlights third-party risk from large IT services providers
summary: A breach at IT services outsourcing giant Wipro, involving an advanced and persistent phishing campaign with zero-day malware, led to its systems being used to target customer accounts. This incident underscores the significant dangers of third-party and supply chain risks, especially with large IT service providers that have extensive access to clients' critical systems. Experts emphasize the necessity of rigorous vetting and ongoing security management for third-party vendors to mitigate such risks.

title: SoFi Select 500 ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the SoFi Select 500 ETF (SFY), including its current price, and basic information like expense ratio, inception date, and the index it tracks. It also offers in-depth analysis on its holdings, performance compared to peers, ESG scores, and technical indicators. The ETF is primarily focused on large-cap growth equities with a significant allocation to technology.

title: ANSYS Cloud: Direct cloud HPC access through ANSYS Mechanical, ANSYS Fluent
summary: ANSYS Cloud provides direct cloud HPC access within ANSYS Mechanical and ANSYS Fluent, leveraging Microsoft Azure for on-demand computing resources. This solution offers built-in, secure, and economical pay-per-use access to HPC, eliminating the need for complex setups or in-house infrastructure. Users can monitor jobs, visualize 3D results in the cloud, and optimize simulation investments with flexible licensing.

title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella featured in today's N150 conversation
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is scheduled for a conversation with Jeff Raikes at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln as part of the university's 150th-anniversary celebration. Nadella's leadership has transformed Microsoft, tripling its market value and accelerating innovation in cloud computing and AI. The event, free and open to the public, will also be streamed live.

title: Verb Purchases Sound Concepts
summary: Verb Technology Co. Inc., an interactive video advertising company, acquired Utah-based video sales company Sound Concepts Inc. for $25 million last week, shortly after Verb's Nasdaq IPO which raised $20.5 million. The acquisition, partly funded by IPO proceeds, removes a competitor and adds 90 employees while Verb plans to open a new office in Newport Beach. CEO Rory Cutaia sees strong growth in the video ad market and is eyeing further acquisitions.

title: IBM/Maersk’s TradeLens adds major carrier ZIM
summary: The TradeLens blockchain shipping solution, a joint venture between Maersk and IBM, has secured a significant win by adding ZIM Integrated Shipping Services, the world’s 11th largest carrier. This addition addresses previous concerns about other shipping lines being hesitant to join due to Maersk's involvement. The platform aims to digitize the documentation process in global trade, emphasizing collaboration and privacy.

title: Sell in May, and Go Away? Maybe At Least Rotate? or Hedge…
summary: This article discusses the "Sell in May and go away" adage for traders, exploring alternatives like rotating into less affected sectors or using inverse/leveraged inverse ETFs. It highlights potential opportunities in healthcare and technology stocks, citing specific companies and Direxion ETFs. The piece emphasizes that traders have choices to navigate seasonal market trends, whether by shifting focus or hedging against potential downturns.

title: Ribbon Session Border Controller (SBC) SWe Lite in the Azure marketplace
summary: Ribbon has made its Session Border Controller (SBC) SWe Lite available in the Azure Marketplace, joining other vendors like AudioCodes and Anynode. This SBC is certified for Teams Direct Routing and caters to small to medium businesses with a low-cost single vCPU Azure VM option, supporting 10 to 1000 employees, with larger options for up to 4000. It offers full voice security and interworking features, simple configuration via a 3-step wizard, and even a no-obligation trial license for potential customers.

title: Robots in the Permian? Climate concerns drive innovation
summary: Oil supermajors like Chevron and Exxon Mobil are heavily investing in the Permian Basin, using advanced automation, cloud computing, and AI to maximize oil extraction. This strategy is seen as a hedge against future climate change regulations and potential drops in oil demand, allowing for quick returns and flexibility. However, environmentalists criticize the focus on fossil fuels, and some experts question the feasibility of the desired automation and the long-term sustainability of shale production.

title: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) earnings Q3 2019
summary: Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT) exceeded revenue and earnings estimates for Q3 2019, causing its shares to rise by 3% in aftermarket hours. The company reported strong growth across its segments, including Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing, driven by demand for cloud offerings and increased engagement in LinkedIn and Xbox Live. Microsoft's CFO highlighted that commercial cloud revenue reached $9.6 billion, marking a 41% year-over-year increase.

title: Here are the executive power moves that help explain everything that's going on in finance, tech and retail
summary: This article details significant executive appointments and promotions across finance, tech, and retail sectors. Key moves include JPMorgan appointing Jennifer Piepszak as CFO and Marianne Lake to CEO of Consumer Lending, Google Cloud hiring former SAP executive Robert Enslin, and Flexport onboarding a Chief Data Officer and Chief Information Security Officer. Best Buy also announced Corie Barry as its first female CEO, and Robinhood made changes to its compliance team, featuring Scott Friedman stepping down and John Castelly taking over as Chief Compliance Officer.

title: AdvisorShares Pure Cannabis ETF (YOLO) Dividend Yield 2026 & History $YOLO
summary: This article provides detailed dividend information for the AdvisorShares Pure Cannabis ETF (YOLO), including its current dividend yield of 1.41% and an annual dividend of $0.04 per share. It outlines the dividend payment history, recent payment dates, and compares YOLO's dividend metrics against other NYSEARCA companies. The report also offers a frequently asked questions section about YOLO's dividend performance.

title: Northern Trust's Data-Driven Transformation: Integrating the Human and Technology Dimensions
summary: Northern Trust, a Fortune 1000 company, is undergoing a data-driven transformation to remain competitive in financial services, focusing on integrating human and technology dimensions for success. Sanjay Saxena, SVP of enterprise data governance, leads this effort, emphasizing data quality, standards, and governance across wealth management, asset management, and asset servicing. The firm leverages advanced technologies like Big Data and AI in partnership with IBM, while also cultivating a strong data culture with clear accountability.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Digital Experience Platforms
summary: This article reviews the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Digital Experience Platforms (DXP), highlighting significant changes and market trends. It discusses the evolution of DXP solutions, the growing importance of AI, machine learning, and cloud-based technology, and analyzes the performance and strategies of 17 key vendors evaluated by Gartner. The piece details which companies have gained or lost ground and what new features are driving their positions in the market.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Integration Platform as a Service
summary: Gartner, Inc. released its 2019 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS), highlighting significant changes and market trends. The report details the strengths and weaknesses of 17 providers, with Informatica and Dell Boomi retaining their leadership positions. The article also notes the entry of new vendors like Software AG and TIBCO Software, and the increasing focus on AI and machine learning capabilities within iPaaS solutions.

title: Sumitomo Mitsui Bank Hires Compliance Guru Andre Burrell to Fix New York Problems
summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. has hired Andre Burrell as managing director and Bank Secrecy Act/anti-money laundering officer for its Americas division to address compliance deficiencies in its New York branch. This appointment follows a written agreement with the U.S. Federal Reserve Board and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to improve its BSA/AML programs. Burrell, a veteran in compliance, will lead the implementation of extensive requirements outlined by the regulators to enhance corporate governance and compliance.

title: Turtle Beach's All-New Recon 70 Series Gaming Headsets For Xbox One & PlayStation 4 Now Available At Retail
summary: Turtle Beach has announced the retail availability of its new Recon 70 series gaming headsets for Xbox One and PlayStation 4, following the successful launch of the Nintendo Switch version. These affordable headsets, priced at $39.95, feature high-quality 40mm speakers, a high-sensitivity flip-up mic, and lightweight comfort, making them a strong contender in the entry-level gaming audio market. The Recon 70 series builds on the success of the Recon 50 series, which has sold over five million units.

title: Cheetah Mobile previews international edition of top-selling CM Translator at Microsoft Build 2019
summary: Cheetah Mobile announced the upcoming international release of its top-selling CM Translator at Microsoft Build 2019. The device, which supports six languages, features an easy-to-use one-button design and a long battery life. CM Translator is powered by AI technology from Microsoft Azure Cognitive Services and Beijing OrionStar, and will retail for $129.99.

title: Starbucks Teams Up With Microsoft To Boost Its Bean-To-Cup Blockchain
summary: Starbucks is partnering with Microsoft to enhance its bean-to-cup blockchain initiative and other technological advancements. This collaboration leverages Microsoft's Azure blockchain cloud services, AI, and IoT to improve supply chain transparency for coffee and introduce features like predictive drive-thru ordering and connected coffee machines across its stores. The partnership aims to provide greater financial opportunities for coffee farmers and solidify Starbucks' position as an innovation leader.

title: Tech Moves: F5 Networks lands former Marketo and J.P. Morgan execs; AI2 adds managing director; Groupon snags REI vet; and more
summary: F5 Networks announced two new senior executives: Mika Yamamoto as EVP and chief marketing & customer experience officer, and Geng Lin as CTO. AI2 appointed Bryan Hale as managing director of its incubator, while Groupon hired REI veteran Craig Rowley as chief marketing officer. The article also details several other notable tech hires and promotions across various Seattle-area companies, including EagleView, Adaptive Biotechnologies, Reverb, Genesys, Olis Robotics, and HNTB Corporation.

title: Zscaler has the world’s largest security cloud
summary: This article discusses Zscaler, a company providing security services with the world's largest security cloud, comprised of 100 data centers. It highlights Zscaler's proprietary technology, its ability to secure cloud migrations through SSL tunnels rather than traditional VPNs, and its extensive data analysis capabilities for early threat detection. The piece also touches on privacy considerations, speed gains, and the future of security in the cloud-first era.

title: Adobe's Path From Boxed Software to SaaS Software And The CIO's Role In That Change
summary: This article chronicles Adobe's journey from a boxed-software company to a SaaS-based software company, highlighting the critical role of CIO Cynthia Stoddard in this transformation. Stoddard discusses modernizing technology, prioritizing customer experience, adopting a cloud-centric DNA, and the importance of architecture in managing legacy systems. She also touches on the increasing importance of AI/ML, operational excellence, and developing female talent in IT.

title: LNG Trailblazer Eisbrenner Dies at 58
summary: Kathleen M. Eisbrenner, a prominent pioneer in the liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry and founder of NextDecade Corporation, has passed away at 58. She was recognized as a leading female executive in the global LNG sector, having also held executive roles at Royal Dutch Shell and founded Excelerate Energy. Her colleagues at NextDecade expressed profound sadness and gratitude for her visionary leadership.

title: Ex-Autonomy CFO jailed for five years over Hewlett-Packard fraud
summary: Sushovan Hussain, former CFO of Autonomy, has been sentenced to five years in prison and fined $4 million for fraud related to the company's $11.1 billion sale to Hewlett-Packard in 2011. He was convicted on 16 counts, including wire fraud and securities fraud, for allegedly inflating Autonomy's financial performance. Hussain is also a defendant in a $5 billion civil fraud trial in London brought by Hewlett-Packard.

title: Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:ESGV)
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF (ESGV), including its current price, key statistics, fund overview, expenses, and recent news headlines. It highlights ESGV's investment strategy, which focuses on U.S. all-cap companies screened for environmental, social, and corporate governance criteria, and lists its top holdings and sector exposure. The fund, managed by Vanguard, has assets under management of $11.58 billion and a net expense ratio of 0.09%.

title: Sempra Energy and partners begin production from Cameron LNG project
summary: Sempra Energy and its partners have commenced production from the Cameron LNG project's first liquefaction train in Hackberry, Louisiana. This milestone is a precursor to the first cargo, expected in the coming weeks, bringing the project closer to delivering 12 million tonnes per annum (Mtpa) of LNG. McDermott International and Chiyoda International were responsible for the engineering, procurement, and construction of the $6bn LNG export facility.

title: Sony Signs Deal With Immersion for Haptic Feedback for VR and Gaming Controllers
summary: Sony has signed a deal with Immersion Corp to license its advanced haptics patent portfolio for gaming and VR controllers, allowing players to feel sensations of pushing, pulling, grasping, and pulsing in games. This agreement comes after past legal disputes between the two companies and Immersion settling other patent litigation. Immersion's CEO, Ramzi Haidamus, noted that the company's transformation is underway, with major litigation behind them and a renewed focus on innovative haptics technologies across various markets.

title: Sony and Microsoft to explore strategic partnership - Source
summary: Sony and Microsoft announced a strategic partnership to explore new cloud-based solutions for gaming experiences and AI. This collaboration will involve joint development in Microsoft Azure for their respective game and content-streaming services, and also includes working on intelligent image sensor solutions and integrating Microsoft's AI platform into Sony consumer products. Both companies aim to enhance entertainment experiences for customers and build better development platforms for content creators.

title: Ayala Foundation, Microsoft launch CodeIT
summary: Ayala Foundation and Microsoft Philippines launched CodeIT, a digital education project aimed at providing underserved Filipino youth access to technology and computer science training. This initiative seeks to bridge the digital divide by equipping 4,000 students and 120 teachers from public elementary schools nationwide with essential skills for the future job market. The program involves training teachers, integrating computer science lessons into the curriculum, and after-hour programs to foster critical thinking and problem-solving skills.

title: Microsoft opens largest AI & IoT lab in Shanghai
summary: Microsoft has opened its largest Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (AI & IoT) Insider Lab in Shanghai, China, in partnership with the state-run Zhangjiang Group. This is Microsoft's fourth and largest such lab globally, aiming to support digital transformation across various industries by leveraging AI and IoT technologies. The lab will provide resources and access to the Microsoft ecosystem for selected Chinese and foreign businesses, with China projected to hold nearly a quarter of the global IoT business exceeding $255 billion by 2022.

title: Microsoft, Sony partner on streaming games, chips and AI
summary: Microsoft and Sony have announced a strategic partnership where Sony will leverage Microsoft's cloud services, specifically Azure, for game and media streaming. The collaboration also extends to co-developing image sensors and integrating Microsoft's AI technology into Sony's consumer products. This deal aims to bolster Microsoft's cloud business and provide Sony's gaming platform with enhanced streaming capabilities, especially as its PlayStation 4 nears the end of its lifecycle.

title: Microsoft opens largest AI & IoT lab in Shanghai
summary: Microsoft Corporation has opened its fourth and largest Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Insider Lab in Shanghai, in partnership with the state-run Zhangjiang Group. The 2,800-square-meter facility in Zhangjiang Hi-Tech Park aims to support digital transformation across various industries by providing hardware, software, cloud services, and access to the Microsoft ecosystem for selected enterprises. This initiative positions China to capture a significant portion of the global IoT market, which is projected to exceed $255 billion by 2022.

title: Cray, the Seattle-based supercomputer pioneer, sold to HPE for $1.3 billion
summary: Seattle-based supercomputer maker Cray has agreed to be acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) for $1.3 billion, or $35 per share, representing a 17.4% premium. This acquisition aims to combine Cray's supercomputing expertise and market position in academia and government with HPE's broader portfolio, bolstering HPE's capabilities in high-end computing and next-generation technology development, especially in the context of cloud computing and AI. The deal, which is subject to shareholder and regulatory approval, is intended to help Cray address challenges of scale and investment in its "exascale" systems roadmap, despite recent contract wins.

title: Wix buys brand promotion agency Gefen Team
summary: Wix.com Ltd. has acquired Tel Aviv-based brand promotion agency Gefen Team to strengthen its brand and help achieve its goal of becoming one of the world's 100 strongest and best-loved brands. Gefen Team's entire staff will join Wix's marketing department, led by Eran Gefen, and will focus on building an international brand. Financial details were not disclosed, but the acquisition is not considered material given Wix's cash reserves of $789 million.

title: Microsoft launches Lagos Development Centre
summary: Microsoft has officially launched its Lagos Development Centre, part of a $100 million investment in Nigeria and Kenya. The center will focus on mixed reality services and aims to develop innovative solutions for both local and global impact, with strong support from the Lagos State Governor-Elect.

title: Top 10 Emerging Skills For The C-Suite
summary: Gartner TalentNeuron data indicates that C-suite executives increasingly require a blend of technical skills, such as advanced-tech knowledge, and soft skills like design thinking. The analysis identifies the top 10 hard and soft skills with the highest emerging demand for C-level roles, including AI, data science, cybersecurity, design thinking, and strategic management. These skills are crucial for navigating rapid digitalization, driving innovation, and effectively understanding and managing customer relations.

title: Digital transformation of Saudi education sector vital in realization of Vision 2030
summary: The digital transformation of Saudi Arabia's education sector is crucial for achieving Vision 2030, with companies like Aruba, a Hewlett Packard Enterprise company, playing a key role in enabling this shift through mobile-first architectures. This transformation aims to enhance student achievement, modernize curricula, and prepare students for future work environments by promoting collaborative, technology-enabled learning experiences. The article highlights the Ministry of Education's "Future Gate" initiative and emphasizes the need for robust, resilient network infrastructure to support pervasive mobile learning and evolving educational technologies.

title: Google to ARM: List of companies that severed ties with Huawei after US ban
summary: Following the US government's ban on Huawei due to national security concerns, a number of major technology companies have severed or suspended ties with the Chinese firm. This article lists companies including Google, ARM Holdings, Microsoft, Lumentum Holdings, Panasonic, Intel, Qualcomm, Xilinx, and Broadcom, as well as organizations like the Wi-Fi Alliance and SD Association, highlighting the significant impact of the ban on Huawei's global operations. The ban initially included a 90-day reprieve for existing products, but future uncertainty remains for Huawei's software and hardware capabilities.

title: Validair: Moving to FMS5 assures monitoring continuity through compatibility
summary: Validair is encouraging customers to upgrade to TSI's FMS5 monitoring software for enhanced functionality, improved user experience, and critical compatibility with modern Microsoft Windows operating systems. The move ensures monitoring continuity, as the older FMS3 version is not supported on current OS versions, posing risks if hardware fails. FMS5 offers features like OPC UA functionality and a more intuitive interface, making it essential for environmental monitoring.

title: Expedia's new 40 acre waterfront campus in Seattle will accommodate 5,000 employees
summary: Expedia Group is opening a new 40-acre waterfront campus in Seattle, designed to accommodate 5,000 employees and enhance recruitment in the competitive tech market. The $900 million campus features biophilic design and aims to reflect the company's dominance in the online travel sector, especially in lodging. This move comes as Expedia, along with Booking Holdings, controls a significant portion of the online travel market, impacting both consumers and independent hotels through commissions.

title: Palo Alto Networks Introduces Prisma: The Secure Way to Cloud
summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Prisma, a new cloud security suite designed to provide simpler, more secure, and comprehensive cloud security. Prisma consolidates and expands on existing cloud security products, offering solutions for secure access, data protection, and application security across various cloud environments. With approximately 9,000 enterprise customers, Prisma aims to be the largest cloud security business globally.

title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Cloud Container Security Provider Twistlock: Report -
summary: Palo Alto Networks has reportedly acquired Twistlock, an Israel-based cybersecurity startup specializing in container, serverless, and public cloud system protection, for an estimated $450 million to $500 million. This acquisition comes just before Palo Alto Networks' Ignite19 conference and follows other strategic moves to expand its MSSP-centric partner program. Twistlock's technology protects major cloud systems like Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Docker, Kubernetes, and Pivotal.

title: Meet the billionaires of the new cloud boom
summary: The growth in cloud software has created a new wave of billionaires, with founders of companies like Atlassian, Zoom, Shopify, and Dropbox amassing significant wealth. This trend highlights investors' interest in "land and expand" business models and recurring revenue, making cloud software a fertile ground for new tech giants. While Salesforce's Marc Benioff was once the dominant figure, many new billionaires now rival or exceed his net worth in the cloud industry.

title: Meet the top seven Indian American CEOs
summary: This article highlights seven prominent Indian American CEOs leading major US companies, whose combined 2018 revenue exceeded $360 billion. It notes the historical rise of Indian American executives in corporate America, starting from the 1990s. The CEOs featured include Sundar Pichai (Google), Satya Nadella (Microsoft), Vivek Sankaran (Albertsons), Sanjay Mehrotra (Micron Technology), Ajay Banga (MasterCard), Shantanu Narayan (Adobe Inc.), and Dinesh Paliwal (Harman International Industries).

title: Inside the Adaptive Biotech IPO: How two brothers built a big idea into a breakthrough company
summary: Adaptive Biotechnologies, founded by brothers Chad and Harlan Robins, is preparing for a $230 million IPO. The company, valued at over $1 billion, aims to revolutionize disease diagnosis and treatment by leveraging the immune system's genetic code, with key partnerships including Microsoft and Genentech. Despite reporting net losses, the biotech firm has a substantial cash reserve and represents a significant development in the Seattle tech and life sciences scene.

title: VGT ETF Down On Tech Stock Woes
summary: The Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) experienced a downturn due to woes in the technology stock market, particularly with the Nasdaq being rattled. The article highlights Apple's decline due to regulatory concerns and mentions the broader risk associated with the concentration of VGT's portfolio in a few major tech companies. Analysts from D.A. Davidson noted increasing regulatory disruption potential for tech titans like Amazon, Apple, Facebook, and Google globally.

title: Microsoft and Oracle to interconnect Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud
summary: Microsoft and Oracle announced a cloud interoperability partnership enabling customers to migrate and run mission-critical enterprise workloads across Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud. This collaboration allows seamless connection of Azure services to Oracle Cloud services, offering a highly optimized "best-of-both-clouds" experience. The partnership provides direct, fast network connectivity, unified identity management, and collaborative support to simplify cloud migrations and deployment of Oracle applications on Azure with Oracle databases in Oracle Cloud.

title: Four emerging app security challenges every CTO needs to know about
summary: SaaS growth and cloud adoption are escalating security risks, making robust protection essential in a GDPR-regulated world. Radware highlights four critical emerging challenges for CTOs: bot management, API protection, DevOps security, and denial-of-service attacks. The article emphasizes the need for machine-learning based solutions and automation to counter sophisticated threats and protect applications across all platforms.

title: Latest update takes Arcserve RHA to the cloud
summary: Arcserve has updated its RHA disaster recovery software, extending its continuous replication capabilities to the cloud. This new version supports site-to-cloud failover, cloud-to-cloud failback, and replication from on-premises environments to public clouds, offering greater flexibility for organizations and enabling application migration to the cloud. The update also introduces Linux support, allowing replication to various hypervisors and cloud platforms like Amazon EC2 and Microsoft Azure, alongside enhanced security features.

title: Jamie Dimon shows the JPMorgan Chase flag at Philly’s big BIO meeting
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon spoke at the BIO 2019 conference in Philadelphia, expressing concerns about the "self-inflicted" U.S.-China trade war and the potential for a broader "economic war." He also discussed his company's expansion in Philadelphia, efforts to cut healthcare costs, and the importance of immigration reform and higher minimum wages. Dimon touched on the soundness of the U.S. financial system despite problematic government policies and the need for stronger leadership and tougher journalists.

title: Commentary: Why Upwork Scratched College Degree Requirements From Our Job Descriptions
summary: Upwork CEO Stephane Kasriel explains why the company removed college degree requirements for all positions. He argues that the rising cost of tuition and the failure of traditional education to keep pace with job market changes are creating a talent gap. The article suggests that businesses should look for alternative ways to identify skilled workers, such as vocational training and apprenticeships, which are more inclusive and relevant to current industry needs.

title: Amazon unveils a chopper-plane mashup to deliver packages
summary: Amazon unveiled a new drone design for its Prime Air fleet, a hybrid helicopter-plane mashup designed for package delivery. The drone features AI and takes off vertically before flying horizontally like a plane. Amazon aims to use these drones for test deliveries of household goods, with the goal of delivering packages within 7.5 miles of a warehouse within 30 minutes, handling items up to five pounds.

title: Keep an Eye on Hybrid Cloud Computing Trend
summary: The Global X Cloud Computing ETF (CLOU), launched less than two months ago, has already attracted $300 million in assets, indicating strong investor interest in cloud computing. The article suggests that CLOU is well-positioned to capitalize on the emerging hybrid cloud trend, which allows businesses to merge public cloud services with their private data centers. Hybrid cloud computing is projected to become a significant market, with estimates valuing it at up to $63 billion.

title: Helping Our Customers Thrive with Digital Technology
summary: Ecolab emphasizes the growing importance of digital technology in enhancing customer value across all industries. The company leverages decades of data and expertise to optimize customer performance, enhance experience, and strengthen field service capabilities through digital solutions like AI, machine learning, and cloud computing. These efforts aim to help customers manage risk, improve outcomes in food, water, and hospital safety, and achieve operational efficiencies.

title: Gartner’s 2019 Magic Quadrant for Disaster Recovery as a Service: Key Takeaways
summary: Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS) report analyzes key providers based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision. The article highlights leaders like Recovery Point, iland, and Microsoft, and discusses the characteristics of Challengers, Visionaries (IBM, Sungard AS), and Niche Players (Flexential, C&W Business, Expedient, TierPoint, BIOS Middle East) in the DRaaS market.

title: Salesforce is buying data visualization company Tableau for $15.7B in all-stock deal
summary: Salesforce announced its acquisition of data visualization company Tableau for $15.7 billion in an all-stock deal. This strategic move aims to enhance Salesforce's analytics capabilities and diversify beyond CRM software, following Google's recent acquisition of Looker. Tableau will operate independently, retaining its headquarters in Seattle and current leadership.

title: Salesforce's $15.7 billion Tableau acquisition: Everything you need to know
summary: Salesforce's $15.7 billion acquisition of Tableau is a strategic move to integrate enterprise data and analytics, aiming to provide a 360-degree view of the customer. The deal is expected to significantly boost Salesforce's revenue while bolstering its data stack capabilities and fending off competitors like Microsoft, SAP, and Oracle. It also leverages Tableau's strong community and academic presence to attract new users to the Salesforce ecosystem.

title: Salesforce swallows Tableau in US$15.3bn buy
summary: Salesforce.com Inc has agreed to acquire big data firm Tableau Software Inc for US$15.3 billion. This acquisition is intended to strengthen Salesforce's position against Microsoft Corp in the market for data analysis and visualization tools, helping businesses target customers more effectively. The deal underscores the growing competition in the market for business intelligence and analytics software.

title: Q&A: Procore CEO Tooey Courtemanche on productivity, technology and the skilled labour gap
