summary: Procore CEO Tooey Courtemanche discusses the evolution of technology adoption in construction, identifying the skilled labor gap, the transition from analog to digital processes, and the need for a collaborative mindset as key challenges. He also highlights how technology can improve productivity and aid in talent recruitment and retention within the industry.

title: Simplify Data Management Across Public or Private Clouds with NetApp Cloud Volumes
summary: NetApp is enhancing data management across public and private clouds by offering a feature-rich portfolio of cloud data services. The article details NetApp's public cloud offerings like Azure NetApp Files, Cloud Volumes Service for Google Cloud and AWS, and Cloud Volumes ONTAP, alongside on-premises solutions such as NetApp HCI and Cloud Volumes Service On-Premises. These solutions aim to provide enterprise-class file services, high performance, and simplified data management, catering to various cloud strategies and regulatory requirements.

title: How Fortune 500 Company CDW Fuels Steady Growth by Focusing on Customers
summary: CDW, a Fortune 500 company, sustains steady growth by prioritizing Customer Experience Management (CXM) and leveraging Adobe Experience Cloud solutions. The company uses Adobe Experience Manager Assets as a digital asset management platform to efficiently deliver valuable content and advice to its 250,000 customers. This approach has led to improved content creation, streamlined workflows, and a focus on personalization to enhance customer experiences and foster loyalty.

title: Pega vs Salesforce: 2022 CRM Software Comparison
summary: This article compares Pega CRM and Salesforce, highlighting their origins, functionalities, and suitable use cases. While Salesforce excels in sales team empowerment and ease of use, Pega CRM offers a more integrated, business process-centric approach with potential long-term cost benefits for digital transformation initiatives. The comparison covers cost, ease of use, implementation, customization, integrations, customer support, and features, providing a detailed analysis for organizations deciding between the two CRM solutions.

title: Fluent acquires AdParlor, a social ad specialist previously owned by Adknowledge, for $10M
summary: Fluent, a marketing company, has acquired AdParlor, a social advertising specialist, for $10 million. AdParlor, originally a major Facebook Ads API vendor, was previously owned by AdKnowledge (now V2 Ventures). This acquisition aims to integrate AdParlor's social media advertising expertise across various platforms into Fluent's existing marketing technology stack.

title: Aruba NetInsight, User Experience Insight coming to Central
summary: Aruba, an HPE company, is integrating its NetInsight and User Experience Insight network analytics tools into its cloud-based Central 2.5 console, which is used to manage Aruba-powered wireless LANs. This integration aims to simplify network management for engineers by centralizing analytics. Additionally, Aruba is introducing a new virtual gateway for Microsoft Azure to enhance its SD-WAN capabilities, strengthening its competition with Cisco in the branch office market.

title: 10 Things You Didn’t Know About Rob Glaser
summary: This article provides 10 interesting facts about Rob Glaser, the founder of RealNetworks and a partner at Accel Partners. It covers aspects of his professional career, including his time at Microsoft and investments, as well as personal details regarding his net worth, charitable work, political support, and family life.

title: Insight Enterprises to Buy PCM in Deal of Massive Channel Proportions
summary: Insight Enterprises is set to acquire PCM Inc. in a deal valued over $580 million, merging two of North America's largest channel organizations. This acquisition aims to boost Insight's momentum in key market segments, accelerate its managed services business, and provide expertise in vertical markets through PCM's 2,700 client-facing professionals. The deal involves Insight paying $35 per share of PCM stock, a 36% premium, with PCM's shares significantly rising after the announcement.

title: Cloud Services Starting To Overtake On-Prem Database Management Systems
summary: A new report by Gartner Inc. indicates that cloud services are rapidly overtaking on-premises solutions in the database management system (DBMS) market, accounting for 68% of the market's 18.4% growth from 2017 to 2018. Gartner predicts that on-premises DBMS will become a "legacy" approach, with significant growth driven by Amazon Web Services and Microsoft's cloud offerings. The shift is attributed to factors like Software as a Service applications, pay-as-you-go pricing, and innovation primarily occurring in cloud DBMS.

title: Can Adobe's Digital Experience Revenues Exceed Digital Media Revenues By 2025?
summary: This article examines whether Adobe's Digital Experience revenues can surpass Digital Media revenues by 2025, noting the former's faster growth rate. While Digital Experience is expanding rapidly, driven by market growth and strategic acquisitions, Digital Media is expected to remain the larger segment through 2025 due to its established market share and steady expansion. The analysis provides detailed forecasts and market share projections for both segments.

title: JPMorgan Chase expands Seattle engineering center to 100 people, plans to add hundreds more
summary: JPMorgan Chase is significantly expanding its technology engineering center in Seattle, growing to 100 people in its first year and signing a new lease to accommodate hundreds more. This expansion is part of the financial services giant's major investment in cloud technology, partnering with AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, and signals Seattle's growing potential as a fintech hub. The bank's CEO, Jamie Dimon, initially skeptical, is now fully committed to cloud adoption and integrating AI into operations.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for CRM Customer Engagement Centers
summary: This article highlights key changes and analyses from the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for CRM Customer Engagement Centers. It discusses how digital business models, AI maturity, and connected customer service ecosystems are shaping the market, with a focus on vendor strengths and weaknesses. The report identifies Salesforce, Pegasystems, and Zendesk as leaders and notes new entrants like Appian.

title: Top 10 Websites in the Middle East and Africa
summary: An infographic from Comscore, Inc. details the top 10 websites in the Middle East and Africa based on October 2012 data, with Google, Facebook, and Microsoft leading in unique visitors. Nearly 135 million people used the internet from home or work across the region. Google secured the top spot with almost 122 million unique visitors, reaching 90% of the digital population.

title: Microsoft, Sony, Nintendo Express Concern Over Trump Tariffs
summary: Microsoft, Sony, and Nintendo have jointly expressed concern over proposed U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods, stating that these would significantly harm the U.S. video game industry, its employees, and consumers. The companies warned that such tariffs would disrupt businesses, increase costs, depress sales, injure stakeholders, and put thousands of U.S. jobs at risk, given that over 96% of consoles imported in 2018 were made in China. They noted that a 25% price increase would make new consoles unaffordable for many families and lead to consumers paying an additional $840 million.

title: PCM Breach: Hackers Gain Microsoft Office 365 Credentials at IT Solutions Provider
summary: IT solutions provider PCM Inc. experienced a cyber incident where hackers stole Microsoft Office 365 administrative credentials for client accounts. This breach, discovered in May 2019, highlights a growing trend of cyberattacks targeting channel partners, MSPs, and solutions providers. PCM stated the impact to its systems and customers was minimal and remediated the issue.

title: Xtrackers S&P 500 Scored & Screened ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:SNPE)
summary: This article provides detailed information about the Xtrackers S&P 500 Scored & Screened ETF (SNPE), including its current price, key statistics, holdings, and recent news. The ETF, launched on June 26, 2019, tracks a principles-selected, market-cap-weighted index of US large-cap securities with a focus on ESG. It highlights the ETF's performance, major shareholders, top holdings like NVIDIA and Microsoft, and expense ratios.

title: Warren Buffett is donating $3.6 billion in Berkshire shares to 5 foundations, including Gates
summary: Warren Buffett is donating $3.6 billion in Berkshire Hathaway shares to five foundations, including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. This involves converting Class A shares into Class B shares, continuing his pledge to give away his wealth throughout his lifetime. Approximately 45% of his 2006 holdings, totaling about $34 billion, have already been donated to these foundations.

title: GIC to Fuel Equinix’s Hyperscale Market Ambition
summary: Equinix, the world’s largest data center provider, is partnering with GIC, Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund, in a $1 billion joint venture to build and operate hyperscale data centers for major digital platforms. This initiative, branded xScale, aims to address the growing demand from tech giants like Alibaba, Amazon, and Microsoft for large-scale data center capacity, especially in Europe. The move allows Equinix to expand into the hyperscale market without cannibalizing its core retail colocation business, leveraging GIC’s capital for significant investments.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Sales Force Automation
summary: The 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Sales Force Automation reveals a 12.8% market growth, with vendors improving AI for data capture and predictive analytics. Key trends include digital optimization driving purchase decisions, SFA being a five-year commitment, and the essential requirement for third-party application integration. The report evaluates 19 providers, noting new additions and removals, and categorizes them into Niche Players, Challengers, Visionaries, and Leaders, with Salesforce topping the Leaders category.

title: Ecolab to invest more on innovation in China
summary: Ecolab Inc., a US-based leader in water, hygiene, and energy technologies, plans to increase its investment in innovation in China and focus on three core business areas. The company aims to more than double its business in China in the medium term, leveraging digital innovation and addressing opportunities in food safety, water management, and healthcare.

title: Juniper Networks wants to simplify cloud access
summary: Juniper Networks is focusing on simplifying cloud access for companies through software-defined networking, addressing the growing complexity of multi-cloud environments. The company proposes a five-step model for a smooth transition to the cloud, emphasizing automation, visibility, and analytics, ultimately aiming for a "Self-Driving Network." Juniper is also collaborating with Nutanix and Red Hat to enhance its cloud solutions and integration capabilities.

title: Microsoft Chairman Among Investors in Telecommunication Startup Drivenets
summary: Microsoft Chairman John Thompson was among several high-profile private investors who backed Israeli networking software startup Drivenets. Drivenets, which emerged from stealth with $110 million in financing, also attracted investments from major tech executives like Steve Luczo of Seagate Technology, Mark McLaughlin (Palo Alto Networks), Pascal Cagni (C4 Ventures), Doug Gilstrap (Ericsson), and Israeli tech investor Benny Schnaider. The company, founded by Ido Susan and Hillel Kobrinsky, develops network management tools for communications service providers.

title: IBM closes $34 billion deal to buy Red Hat to boost cloud business
summary: IBM has completed its $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat Inc., marking its largest-ever deal, to significantly bolster its cloud computing business. This strategic move aims to help companies transition to hybrid cloud environments, offering a mix of public and private cloud applications. Red Hat will operate as a distinct unit within IBM, maintaining its headquarters and management, with no immediate job or cost cuts planned.

title: You’re Hired. Now Wear This Headset to Learn the Job. (Published 2019)
summary: Kenworth is using Microsoft HoloLens headsets to train new employees for assembling semitruck cabs, significantly reducing the time it takes for workers to learn new tasks. This new high-tech training method, which overlays digital instructions onto the real world, is proving more engaging and efficient than traditional observation-based training. Paccar, Kenworth's parent company, plans to expand the use of these devices across its plants.

title: IBM mainframes face competitive pressures inside and out
summary: IBM's mainframe business is facing increasing competitive pressure from cloud-based solutions and even its own Power servers, despite strong legacy customer loyalty. While IBM continues to invest in mainframe modernization, analysts debate its long-term strategic emphasis given the company's focus on cloud, analytics, and other distributed platforms. The article highlights migrations of mainframe workloads to the cloud by companies like Swisscom and Sabre Corp, and discusses the challenges of cost, agility, and skills shortages affecting mainframe adoption, alongside IBM's efforts to innovate and maintain market relevance.

title: L Squared and Microsoft Corporation Reach New Partnership Agreement
summary: L Squared Digital Signage and Microsoft Corp. have established a new IP Co-Sell Ready partner agreement, integrating L Squared's digital signage solutions with Microsoft's Azure and IoT Hub. This partnership grants L Squared sales and marketing advantages, co-branding, and direct sales support, highlighting their technical proficiency and successful market presence. The L Squared Hub platform integrates with various Microsoft solutions, providing enhanced internal communication for customers and expanding business opportunities through Microsoft's global sales executives.

title: Cloud Volumes ONTAP: Experience the Benefits of ONTAP Across Azure, AWS, and GCP
summary: NetApp has expanded its Cloud Volumes ONTAP (CVO) offering to include Google Cloud Platform (GCP), making it available across all three major cloud providers: Microsoft Azure, Amazon AWS, and Google Cloud Platform. CVO offers full ONTAP features in the cloud, enabling use cases like multi-cloud disaster recovery, cost-efficient storage for cloud-native applications, and persistent storage for Docker and Kubernetes. The article differentiates CVO (IaaS, user-managed) from Cloud Volumes Service (CVS) (PaaS, fully managed).

title: Microsoft Word passes 1 billion installs on Play Store
summary: Microsoft Word has become the company's first Android app to surpass 1 billion installs on the Google Play Store. While this number includes pre-installations on devices from manufacturers like Samsung, it signifies a major milestone for Microsoft's mobile productivity suite. This achievement highlights the continued popularity of traditional office software alongside cloud-based alternatives.

title: Investors Use Indexes to Play in the Video Game Business (Published 2019)
summary: The video game industry, transitioning from arcades to mobile and streaming, presents significant investment opportunities. Big tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and Amazon are entering the streaming video game market, alongside equipment makers and game publishers set to capitalize on new capabilities. The industry is projected to reach $180 billion in annual sales, with investors increasingly using exchange-traded funds to gain exposure.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Multiexperience Development Platforms
summary: Gartner has released its inaugural Magic Quadrant for Multiexperience Development Platforms (MXDP), evolving from previous Mobile App Development Platforms (MADPs) to address progressive web, conversational, immersive, and wearable apps. The report evaluates 13 key providers, categorizing them into Niche Players, Challengers, Visionaries, and Leaders based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision. OutSystems, Mendix, Oracle, Progress, Kony, and Salesforce are highlighted as Leaders, with Microsoft leading the Challengers.

title: H&M, Microsoft, PVH Corp collaborate in circular fashion initiative
summary: H&M, Microsoft, and PVH Corp are collaborating on CircularID, an initiative to establish a global standard for tracking fashion products to support rental, resale, and recycling. This project, coordinated by Eon, aims to provide unique digital identities for garments with embedded information like materials, origin, and recycling instructions, throughout their lifecycle. CircularID is designed to encourage circularity by helping re-commerce scale and inspiring new business models for brands.

title: Vungle acquired by Blackstone for reported $750M
summary: Blackstone Group is acquiring mobile video advertisement startup Vungle for a reported $750 million. This acquisition provides Vungle with stronger financial backing and allows the company to move past a wrongful termination lawsuit with its co-founder, Zain Jaffer. The deal reflects the significant growth in the mobile video advertising market.

title: AT&T and Microsoft announce a strategic alliance to deliver innovation with cloud, AI and 5G
summary: AT&T and Microsoft have formed a multiyear strategic alliance to accelerate AT&T's public cloud transformation and deliver new customer offerings using cloud, AI, and 5G. Microsoft will become the preferred cloud provider for AT&T's non-network applications, with AT&T migrating most of these workloads to the public cloud by 2024 and adopting Microsoft 365. The collaboration aims to innovate in areas like edge computing, 5G, IoT, and cybersecurity, while also addressing social good initiatives.

title: Target Nabs Former Facebook Manager Hari Govind
summary: Target Corp. has appointed Hari Govind, formerly a group manager at Facebook, as its senior vice president of infrastructure and operations for its technology team. In this new role, Govind will oversee digital infrastructure and technology across Target's various operations, leveraging his over two decades of experience to enhance the retailer's technological capabilities. This appointment aligns with Target's ongoing strategy to prioritize digital integration and technology in its business model.

title: Microsoft, AT&T sign cloud deal worth more than $2 billion
summary: Microsoft and AT&T have signed a multi-year cloud deal valued at over $2 billion, making Microsoft AT&T's "preferred" cloud vendor. AT&T will utilize Microsoft's Azure cloud service and Microsoft 365 for its workforce and will collaborate with Microsoft on edge computing for its 5G network. This agreement marks a significant shift for AT&T towards a "public cloud first" strategy and strengthens Microsoft's position in the competitive cloud services market.

title: Louis Vuitton Owner Bernard Arnault Replaces Microsoft’s Bill Gates as World’s 2nd Richest Person
summary: Bernard Arnault, owner of Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessy (LVMH), has surpassed Bill Gates to become the world's second-richest person according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Arnault's net worth rose to US$107.6 billion due to a US$39 billion gain in 2019 alone, pushing Gates to the third position. This shift highlights the significant wealth accumulation of top billionaires.

title: Microsoft Earnings Beat Puts Cloud Computing ETF in Spotlight
summary: Microsoft's strong second-quarter earnings, including an EPS of $1.37 against forecasts of $1.21, significantly outpaced analyst expectations, largely driven by its cloud computing segment. This segment, led by Azure's 64% annualized growth, has now surpassed core productivity for the first time in three years, highlighting the increasing demand for cloud solutions. This surge in cloud adoption is putting Global X Cloud Computing ETF (Nasdaq: CLOU) in the spotlight, as the cloud computing industry is projected to grow from $188 billion in 2018 to over $300 billion by 2022.

title: eBay Welcomes Pete Thompson as Chief Product Officer; Mazen Rawashdeh promoted to Chief Technology Officer
summary: eBay announced new leadership appointments, welcoming Pete Thompson as Senior Vice President and Chief Product Officer and promoting Mazen Rawashdeh to Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer. Both executives will report to President and CEO Devin Wenig, with Thompson focusing on personalizing the shopping experience and Rawashdeh leading platform engineering and architecture. Additionally, Scott Gaffney joins as VP, Search Engineering, and Steve Metz returns as VP, Product Analytics, further strengthening eBay's leadership in product and technology.

title: OpenAI forms exclusive computing partnership with Microsoft to build new Azure AI supercomputing technologies
summary: OpenAI and Microsoft have formed an exclusive multiyear computing partnership, with Microsoft investing $1 billion. The collaboration aims to build new Azure AI supercomputing technologies and a platform for OpenAI to create advanced AI technologies, ultimately working towards artificial general intelligence (AGI). Microsoft will become OpenAI's preferred partner for commercializing new AI technologies, with a shared commitment to ethical and trustworthy AI deployment.

title: ServiceNow (NOW) Q2 2019 earnings results
summary: ServiceNow reported strong Q2 2019 earnings, with a 32% jump in revenues to $833.9 million and net income rising to 71 cents per share, surpassing analyst projections. Despite these positive results, the company's shares fell 5% post-market due to valuation concerns. ServiceNow also provided an optimistic outlook for subscription revenue and billings growth for Q3 and the full year 2019, driven by cloud adoption and strategic partnerships.

title: Apple Is Now the Most Valuable Brand Ever, Thanks to This 1 Thing. (The Good News Is You Can Totally Do It Too)
summary: Apple has become the most valuable brand globally, valued at $205 billion, largely due to its commitment to delighting customers beyond expectations. While the iPhone's success contributes, the core reason for its brand value lies in fostering positive feelings through every customer interaction. The article suggests that any business can achieve similar brand success by focusing on unexpected customer delight rather than just meeting expectations.

title: 10 Things You Didn’t Know about Tractor Supply CEO Gregory A. Sandfort
summary: This article details 10 facts about Gregory A. Sandfort, the CEO of Tractor Supply Company since December 2012. It covers his extensive retail experience, educational background at the University of Louisville, previous roles at The Michaels Companies, Inc., and his current board memberships. The piece also highlights his key contributions to Tractor Supply, including his understanding of consumer preferences and role in the omni-channel strategy.

title: Report: Amazon Web Services Expands in Herndon
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is expanding its presence in Northern Virginia by leasing 13820 Sunrise Valley Drive in Herndon, adding to its significant footprint in the region. This expansion comes as AWS continues to pursue major federal government contracts, including the Department of Defense's $10 billion JEDI cloud contract. The company has leased close to 852,800 square feet in Northern Virginia, cementing its status as one of the fastest-growing tenants.

title: SoftBank Group's $108 billion Vision Fund 2 draws in Microsoft, Apple
summary: SoftBank Group announced commitments of approximately $108 billion for its second Vision Fund, aimed at investing in technology firms, with Microsoft and Apple among the new investors. The Japanese conglomerate itself plans to invest $38 billion. Notably, the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia and Abu Dhabi, key investors in the first fund, were absent from the initial list, though discussions with them were ongoing.

title: Gartner Says Worldwide IaaS Public Cloud Services Market Grew 31.3% in 2018
summary: The worldwide Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) market experienced significant growth in 2018, increasing by 31.3% to reach $32.4 billion. Amazon maintained its position as the leading vendor, followed by Microsoft, Alibaba, Google, and IBM, indicating a consolidation trend favoring major providers who can invest heavily in scalable data center infrastructure and offer a rich feature set.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise announces new Managing Director for HPE SA
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has appointed President Ntuli as the new Managing Director for HPE South Africa, effective August 1st, 2019. Ntuli brings 18 years of IT experience, having previously worked at Dimension Data MEA and spent over six years at HPE earlier in his career. In his new role, Ntuli will oversee HPE's hardware, software, and services portfolio, focusing on growth and customer satisfaction in South Africa.

title: Skype for Business Online 3PIP IP Phones will work with Microsoft Teams until July 31st 2023
summary: Microsoft announced that 3rd Party IP (3PIP) phones certified for Skype for Business Online will continue to function with Microsoft Teams, albeit with limited functionality, until July 31, 2023. An update released on August 3, 2020, extended this support beyond 2023. This article clarifies the implications for users migrating from Skype for Business Online or Server who use these devices, noting that this applies to 3PIP phones and not newer Microsoft Teams IP Phones.

title: ScanSource acquires intY
summary: ScanSource, Inc., a global provider of technology products, has acquired Bristol-based cloud services distributor intY and its CASCADE platform. This acquisition aims to simplify the sale of strategic cloud services for ScanSource partners, including offerings from Microsoft, Symantec, and Acronis, by providing tools for provisioning, analytics, and recurring revenue generation. Both companies expressed confidence that the integration will offer compelling solutions to the market.

title: Dynatrace’s Stock Climbed 49% In Market Debut. Its CEO Recalls How A Dinner In Austria Put The Gears In Motion
summary: Dynatrace's stock soared 49% in its market debut, pushing its valuation to $6.7 billion, making it a success in the year's software industry IPOs. The company's CEO, John Van Siclen, revealed that a dinner four years prior in Linz, Austria, led to a strategic pivot towards cloud-based software, which significantly boosted its market position. Despite a $1 billion debt burden from a private equity spin-off, investors were reportedly comfortable due to Dynatrace's strong free cash flow and increasing subscription revenue.

title: Janus Henderson U.S. Sustainable Equity ETF (SSPX) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
summary: This page provides an overview of the Janus Henderson U.S. Sustainable Equity ETF (SSPX), including its current stock price, recent performance data, and key holdings. The ETF aims to invest in 30-50 U.S.-tied equity securities, primarily larger companies, with a focus on sustainable equities. It also lists related ETF news and research reports.

title: Could Amazon Lose the Pentagon JEDI Project?
summary: The Pentagon's new Secretary of Defense Mike Esper announced a review of the bidding process for the $10 billion JEDI cloud computing contract, raising concerns for Amazon. This review follows protests from Oracle and IBM, as well as doubts expressed by President Trump about the competitive bidding process. The news caused Amazon's stock to slide, highlighting the significance of the contract and the political scrutiny surrounding it.

title: Russian hacking group STRONTIUM attacking corporate IoT devices, Microsoft says
summary: Microsoft's Threat Intelligence Center has reported that the state-backed Russian hacking group STRONTIUM has been attacking corporate IoT devices. These attacks exploited insecure IoT devices, such as printers, VOIP phones, and video decoders, which often had default passwords or unpatched software, to gain initial access to corporate networks and then move laterally to seek higher-value data. Security experts highlight the inherent insecurity of many IoT devices as a significant risk to organizations.

title: J2 Group, with Microsoft Corporation sets up in Gozo Innovation Hub...
summary: The government of Malta is fostering economic development and competitiveness in Gozo through innovation, entrepreneurship, and training opportunities, particularly in the tech sector. This initiative has led to J2 Group, in partnership with Microsoft Corporation, establishing operations in the Gozo Innovation Hub in Xewkija. This move aims to create high-quality jobs, develop a skilled workforce, and position Gozo as a center for excellence in areas like AI, machine learning, and data analytics.

title: Refinery could be sued over toxic waste
summary: Environmental groups are moving to sue Phillips 66 over allegations of years of mismanaging hazardous waste at its Wilmington and Carson facilities, which they claim puts South Bay residents at risk. This legal action follows concerns first raised by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency four years ago and frustration with what advocates describe as lax oversight by federal and state regulators. The environmentalists are particularly concerned about a leak of toxic selenium waste and the EPA's recent decrease in enforcement actions.

title: Walmart Pulls Violent Game Displays; No Change on Gun Sales
summary: Following a mass shooting at one of its stores, Walmart has instructed employees to remove all signs, displays, and videos that depict violence, including turning off video game consoles showing violent games and hunting videos. However, the retailer has not changed its policy on selling video games that depict violence or its gun sales policy, a decision that has drawn criticism from politicians like Senator Elizabeth Warren. This action comes amidst a rise in mass shootings across the U.S. and a national debate on gun control.

title: What's Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms
summary: Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms (LCAPs) evaluates 18 significant providers, highlighting the market's growth due to developer shortages and the demand for democratized app development. The report details the performance of key vendors like Salesforce, Microsoft, OutSystems, Mendix, and Appian, noting shifts in their quadrant positions and their contributions to the evolving LCAP landscape. New additions include K2 and ProntoForms, reflecting the dynamic nature of this critical enterprise technology sector.

title: The Gartner 2019 Magic Quadrant for Unified Endpoint Management Tools
summary: This article discusses Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Unified Endpoint Management Tools, defining UEM and highlighting key capabilities and trends. It analyzes the positioning of various vendors, noting shifts in Challengers, Niche Players, Visionaries, and particularly the rise of Citrix to the Leaders quadrant, alongside MobileIron, BlackBerry, IBM, Microsoft, and VMware. The report emphasizes the increasing importance of CMT integration and the evolving UEM market.

title: GIC Aims for the Cloud in China Data Centre Tie-Up with GDS
summary: GIC, Singapore's sovereign wealth fund, has partnered with GDS Holdings to build and operate hyperscale data centers in China, including second-tier cities, for a leading internet and cloud service provider. This collaboration involves GIC acquiring 90 percent equity in project companies, with GDS retaining 10 percent and continuing operations, marking GIC's latest investment in data centers globally. The partnership aims to support the digital transformation in China, leveraging GDS's expertise and GIC's financial backing, despite GDS's history of net losses.

title: Microsoft is a leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Unified Endpoint Management, 2019
summary: Microsoft has been positioned as a leader in Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) Tools, Worldwide, based on its completeness of vision and ability to execute. The company highlights its extensive product integration, particularly with System Center Configuration Manager and Office 365 mobile apps, as key strengths. Microsoft emphasizes the importance of cloud-scale insights and connection for modern management tools, noting that Intune and ConfigMgr manage over 175 million devices globally, contributing to a robust data set for continuous improvement.

title: Descartes MacroPoint real-time visibility platform migrates to Azure SQL Database to support growth and improve flexibility
summary: Descartes migrated its MacroPoint real-time visibility platform to Azure SQL Database to enhance flexibility and support growth. This move allowed Descartes to better focus resources on product innovation, scale effectively for fluctuating demands, and leverage advanced features like built-in high availability and automated backups offered by Azure's Business Critical tier. The successful migration has also spurred new public cloud projects and the deployment of AI-related solutions within the company.

title: Leading The Farm Into The Future
summary: Livestock Improvement Corporation (LIC), a New Zealand agri-tech co-operative, successfully migrated its products and services to Microsoft Azure to enhance productivity and meet growing demands. This digital transformation, executed within six months and before the peak dairy season, allowed LIC to leverage cloud benefits like scalability, cost-effectiveness, and improved security. The move enables LIC to build infrastructure aligned with Scaled Agile and DevOps practices, supporting advanced research and adapting to seasonal business needs more efficiently.

title: Data-Center Market Is Booming Amid Shift to Cloud
summary: The data-center market is experiencing a boom driven by the shift to cloud computing, even as many businesses shed their own facilities. This trend is leading to increased deals and consolidation among data-center landlords and cloud providers as they seek more capacity. Companies like Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. are major drivers of this demand for co-location services.

title: Metro Phoenix's west side to land 300 new distribution jobs by end of next year
summary: Chino, California-based Quetico is establishing a distribution center in Goodyear, Arizona, which is expected to create 300 new jobs by the end of 2020. The company purchased nearly 40 acres near the Phoenix Goodyear Airport, citing the location's connectivity and competitive business costs. This addition continues a trend of job growth in Goodyear, following announcements from Nike, Chewy Inc., UPS Inc., Ball Corp., and Microsoft.

title: Zoom's founder left a 6-figure job because he wasn't happy—and following his heart made him a billionaire
summary: Eric Yuan, founder and CEO of Zoom, left a high-paying executive job at Cisco to pursue his vision for a better videoconferencing platform despite initial skepticism. His decision, driven by unhappiness with his previous role and a desire to innovate, led him to build Zoom into a company with a market valuation of roughly $42 billion, making him a billionaire with a 22% stake worth over $9 billion. The article highlights his journey from a young immigrant with visa struggles to a tech mogul, emphasizing the importance of passion and customer satisfaction in his success.

title: Gartner names Microsoft a Leader in 2019 Endpoint Protection Platforms Magic Quadrant
summary: Gartner has named Microsoft a Leader in its 2019 Endpoint Protection Platforms Magic Quadrant, recognizing the company's strong capabilities in execution and vision. Microsoft attributes this achievement to its continuous evolution of Microsoft Defender Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) and its commitment to providing best-in-class protection against sophisticated threats. The article highlights key features of Microsoft Defender ATP, such as multi-layered protection, threat analytics, and automated security, that contributed to this high ranking.

title: Copyright case: Media Rights Technologies Inc. v. Microsoft Corp., USA
summary: A US Court of Appeals mostly affirmed the dismissal of a copyright infringement suit brought by Media Rights Technologies, Inc. (MRT) against Microsoft, based on claim preclusion from a prior patent infringement suit. However, the court reversed the dismissal for copyright infringement claims concerning products sold by Microsoft after MRT filed its original patent infringement suit, arguing that new sales constituted new violations. This allows MRT to pursue claims for sales occurring after April 25, 2013.

title: President Moon bets his own money on a Korean victory in trade spat with Japan
summary: South Korean President Moon Jae-in will invest in the NH-Amundi Victorious Korea Equity Fund, which supports local companies amidst a trade dispute with Japan. This fund focuses on Korean suppliers that could benefit from Japan's export curbs on key semiconductor materials. This move echoes a past presidential investment to promote economic agendas and aims to reduce South Korea's reliance on external factors for its manufacturing industry.

title: Blue Ocean acquires Beam telepresence robot from Suitable Technologies
summary: Blue Ocean Robotics ApS has acquired all assets and rights for the Beam telepresence robot from Suitable Technologies Inc., expanding its portfolio of award-winning robots. Blue Ocean Robotics, which previously partnered with Suitable Technologies as a main reseller, aims to further commercialize Beam on an international stage, citing significant growth potential in the mobile telepresence robot market. The acquisition is expected to enhance production, development, sales, and support for Beam, with a focus on applications in healthcare, remote work, and education.

title: Red Hat CEO Says Acquisition by IBM Will Help Spur More Open-Source Innovation
summary: Red Hat CEO Jim Whitehurst stated that IBM's acquisition of Red Hat will foster more open-source innovation, emphasizing a collaborative "two cultures working together" approach. The acquisition aims to strengthen IBM's cloud business by enabling customers to use Red Hat's open-source software across various cloud providers, including IBM's own cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure. Red Hat's technology helps CIOs run applications both in their own data centers and across third-party cloud services, enhancing flexibility and reducing risk.

title: HPE Takes VMware Cloud Users On Its Synergy Journey To Greenlake
summary: HPE is expanding its GreenLake cloud-like IT consumption model by partnering with VMware to integrate GreenLake and HPE Synergy with VMware Cloud Foundation. This collaboration allows joint customers to run VMware Cloud Foundation as a service on GreenLake, offering a cloud-like experience with greater flexibility and cost efficiency in their own datacenters. The initiative is part of HPE's ambitious plan to deliver its entire portfolio as a service by 2022, leveraging GreenLake's metering and capacity management capabilities to optimize IT environments.

title: DOD awards $7.6B Microsoft Office 365 cloud contract to General Dynamics and partners
summary: The U.S. Defense Department has awarded a $7.6 billion, 10-year contract to General Dynamics Corp. subsidiary CSRA LLC, in partnership with Dell Technologies Inc. and Minburn Technology Group LLC, to standardize its email and collaboration workflows on Microsoft's Office 365. This Defense Enterprise Office Solutions (DEOS) program aims to migrate 1.5 million users to Office 365, with an initial focus on moving personnel off the aging Defense Enterprise Email system. The contract also highlights the requirement for Impact Level 6 certification for Secret-level data, which Microsoft is reportedly still obtaining, using its recently authorized Azure cloud regions.

title: The Power of Scarcity
summary: This article discusses the concept of scarcity and its impact on value, using examples from the Popeyes chicken sandwich phenomenon, gold, municipal bonds, and share dilution. It also delves into the current economic climate, including the U.S.-China trade war, its effects on various markets, and global economic indicators for different sectors and regions. The author highlights both opportunities and threats in the precious metals, energy, emerging markets, and blockchain sectors.

title: Groceries And Gadgets: The Robots Coming To A Supermarket Near You
summary: This article discusses the increasing presence of robots in supermarkets like Walmart and Stop & Shop, used for tasks such as inventory monitoring, cleaning spills, and unloading trucks. The implementation of these robots raises questions about their impact on labor, with companies like Walmart stating they aim to reallocate employees to customer-focused roles rather than replacing them entirely. Union representatives and technology developers weigh in on the implications of this automation for workers and efficiency in the retail industry.

title: Elastic Launches Elasticsearch Service on Microsoft Azure
summary: Elastic N.V. announced the launch of Elasticsearch Service on Microsoft Azure, providing a fully managed Elasticsearch and Kibana service for Azure users. This collaboration enhances the experience for users of both the Elastic Stack and Microsoft products, offering features like Elastic APM, SIEM, and machine learning, alongside regular updates and security patches. The service is initially available in public beta in two Azure regions, with plans for general availability and enhanced support later in 2019.

title: Walgreens Boots Alliance nabs CIO from Kraft Heinz
summary: Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) has appointed Francesco Tinto as its new global chief information officer and senior vice president, effective September 6, 2019. Tinto, formerly the global CIO at Kraft Heinz Company, will lead WBA's global IT strategy during a period focused on digital transformation and cost reduction. His appointment comes as WBA aims to invest in digitalization capabilities and strengthen key partnerships, including a significant seven-year deal with Microsoft.

title: IFA 2019: Presenting SoftPOS – A Solution that Turns Smartphones and Tablets into a Contactless Payment Terminal
summary: First Data (now Fiserv), Visa, and Samsung Electronics are showcasing their new SoftPOS solution at IFA 2019, which transforms smartphones and tablets into contactless payment terminals without additional equipment. This technology enables contactless transactions of any amount using embedded NFC functionality on mobile devices, accepting payments from cards, other NFC-enabled phones, or wearables. A pilot program for SoftPOS will launch in Poland by the end of 2019, with plans for expansion to EMEA and APAC regions.

title: Adobe's Omniture purchase a decade ago, set stage for cloud shift, Experience Cloud
summary: This article reflects on Adobe's acquisition of Omniture a decade ago, highlighting how it was a pivotal moment for the company's shift to a cloud and subscription-based model. Initially met with skepticism from Wall Street and even some Omniture employees, CEO Shantanu Narayen's vision of connecting creativity, content, and data laid the groundwork for Adobe's current Experience Cloud and its broader enterprise software strategy. The move, though painful financially at first, ultimately provided a blueprint for other software vendors transitioning to the cloud.

title: Technology firms vie for billions in data-analytics contracts
summary: The article discusses the booming data-analytics market, highlighting companies like C3.ai and Databricks that are vying for billions in contracts. It details the journey of C3.ai's founder, Tom Siebel, and the industry's potential to revolutionize business productivity, despite current challenges in implementing truly sophisticated AI platforms. The piece also notes the significant financial valuations and growth projections for the data analytics sector.

title: Ford sells monthly vehicle subscription service to Fair
summary: Fair, a vehicle subscription startup, has agreed to acquire Ford Motor's vehicle subscription service, Canvas, for an undisclosed amount, marking significant growth for Fair and another exit from an emerging mobility business for Ford. This acquisition will nearly double Fair's engineering capabilities and enable rapid expansion, while subscribers of Canvas will have the opportunity to join Fair. Ford's sale of Canvas is part of its $11 billion restructuring plan and follows the shedding of another mobility unit, Chariot, earlier in the year.

title: Taking a Look Under the Hood of VanEck’s Video Gaming and Esports ETF
summary: This article provides an in-depth look at the holdings within VanEck's Video Gaming and Esports ETF (ESPO), highlighting key companies from both Asia-Pacific and the U.S. It discusses the performance and business models of leading firms like Sea Limited, Bandai Namco, Square Enix, Advanced Micro Devices, Zynga, and Activision Blizzard. The article suggests that investing in a diversified ETF can offer targeted exposure to the high-growth video gaming and esports sector.

title: Bill Gates Told Me This 25 Years Ago and It’s Still Freakin’ Brilliant
summary: The author recounts an interview with Bill Gates from 25 years ago where Gates shared his philosophy on leadership during a critical time for Microsoft. Gates emphasized nurturing a corporate culture that fosters creative thinking, employee development, and delegation to small teams, believing that financial success would naturally follow. This strategy allowed Microsoft to successfully pivot and expand into multiple new markets while maintaining its core business.

title: Schlumberger, Chevron and Microsoft Announce Collaboration to Accelerate Digital Transformation
summary: Schlumberger, Chevron, and Microsoft have announced a three-party collaboration to accelerate the creation of innovative petrotechnical and digital technologies. This partnership aims to build Azure-native applications within the DELFI cognitive E&P environment to process, visualize, and interpret data from multiple sources, enhancing insights for Chevron. The initiative focuses on accelerating the industry's digital transformation, leveraging cloud and AI to address energy challenges, including sustainability.

title: The ‘new rules’ of employability demand agility, determination
summary: The rules of employability are shifting, with employers prioritizing a mix of skills and behaviors like communication, problem-solving, digital proficiency, and especially agility and drive over traditional credentials. This demand for adaptability and soft skills is also influencing higher education, which is increasingly partnering with industry to better prepare graduates for a less hierarchical and more technology-driven workforce.

title: Introducing HP Elite Dragonfly—the ultralight PC designed for the mobile workforce
summary: HP Inc. has introduced the HP Elite Dragonfly, an ultralight PC designed for mobile business professionals. This new device weighs under one kilogram, runs on Windows 10 Pro, and offers up to 24.5 hours of battery life. It also features Wi-Fi 6 connectivity and HP Sure Sense for enhanced security against malware attacks.

title: The highest-paying company in 2019 pays a median salary of $170,929 — here are 9 other companies that pay the most
summary: Glassdoor compiled a list of the 25 highest-paying companies in 2019, with a focus on the top 10. These companies, primarily in tech, consulting, and finance, offer median employee salaries of $148,000 or above. Palo Alto Networks leads the list with a median staff salary of $170,929.

title: Interview with Chuck Noski and Helmut Panke, Microsoft board of directors
summary: Chuck Noski and Helmut Panke, two long-serving members of Microsoft's board of directors, discuss their 16 years with the company. They share insights on how they joined the board, its evolving role in strategy and oversight, and unique challenges faced as chairs of the Audit and Regulatory & Public Policy Committees, respectively. The interview highlights Microsoft's transformation, its commitment to stakeholders, and emphasizes the importance of diverse perspectives and ethical considerations in technology.

title: Las Vegas Sands moves to strengthen China ties with appointment of Microsoft executive Yan Xuan
summary: Las Vegas Sands (LVS) has appointed Microsoft Corporation’s Global Vice President, Yan Xuan, to its board of directors. This strategic move is likely intended to protect LVS's interests in Macau amidst ongoing US-China trade tensions and the impending re-tendering of Macau casino concessions in 2022. Yan Xuan previously held senior leadership positions in China with other global technology firms and will receive an annual retainer of US$150,000.

title: Microsoft customers gain a financial services advocate in new CVP Bill Borden
summary: Microsoft has appointed Bill Borden as Corporate Vice President of Financial Services, leveraging his 20 years of industry experience from Bank of America Merrill Lynch and Citigroup. Borden will lead Microsoft's go-to-market strategy in financial services, focusing on digital transformation and empowering intelligent banking solutions. His appointment underscores Microsoft's investment in industry-specific expertise to better serve its customers.

title: Avantis U.S. Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:AVUS)
summary: The Avantis U.S. Equity ETF (AVUS) is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the Russell 3000 index, launched on September 24, 2019, and managed by American Century Investments. It features a diversified portfolio of US equities with a bias towards smaller, more profitable, or value companies. As of January 9, 2026, AVUS was trading at $115.05, with $10.80 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.15%.

title: More $10 billion software companies are being minted than ever before — here's why
summary: The year 2019 has seen an unprecedented number of cloud software companies reaching a $10 billion market capitalization, with Datadog, Zoom, Slack, and Crowdstrike leading the charge due to high customer retention rates. This trend indicates investors' hunger for high-growth technology companies with strong financials, even as they shy away from cash-burning consumer businesses. However, the high valuations also present risks as early investors may look to cash out their gains.

title: The owner of the New York Stock Exchange is now in the Bitcoin business
summary: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), owner of the NYSE, has launched Bakkt, a digital asset marketplace offering physically-settled Bitcoin futures contracts. This move is seen as a significant step towards mainstream adoption of digital assets and aims to make institutions less skeptical of cryptocurrencies through a regulated and transparent platform. Bakkt differentiates itself by settling contracts with actual Bitcoin, unlike CME Group's cash-settled futures, and includes a Bitcoin "warehouse" to store digital coins.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for CRM Lead Management
summary: This article provides an analysis of the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for CRM Lead Management, highlighting key changes and trends. It discusses the importance of analytics, content management, and sales/marketing coordination in lead management, and evaluates the strengths of 15 significant providers across the four quadrants. The report also notes new entrants, significant movements, and specific functionalities of leading vendors like Oracle, Marketo, Salesforce, and Creatio.

title: Phishing attacks abusing appspot.com and web.app domains on Google Cloud
summary: Zscaler ThreatLabZ has identified a rise in phishing attacks leveraging Google’s Appspot.com and Web.app domains. These sophisticated campaigns utilize SSL certificates from Google and employ well-designed login pages to spoof brands like Dropbox, Microsoft, and DocuSign, aiming to steal user credentials. The attackers use evasion techniques, including external JavaScript files, to bypass detection by analysis engines.

title: Wells Fargo appoints Charles Scharf as new CEO
summary: Wells Fargo has appointed Charles Scharf as its new CEO, making him the third chief executive in as many years, as the bank attempts to move past a series of scandals. Scharf will take over from C. Allen Parker on October 21st, after the bank has faced issues including millions of fake checking accounts and a $1 billion fine from federal regulators. Wall Street reacted positively to the news, with Wells Fargo shares rising almost 3%.

title: Avantis U.S. Equity ETF
summary: This page provides a comprehensive profile of the Avantis U.S. Equity ETF (AVUS), including its price, dividend and valuation, expense ratio, holdings, performance, and ESG scores. It details the ETF's structure (Active ETF), inception date (September 24, 2019), and asset under management (AUM) of $11,023.0 M, offering a deep dive into its characteristics relative to other ETFs in its category and segment. The article also presents various charts, technical analysis, and comparisons to assist investors and financial advisors in evaluating AVUS.

title: Five Questions with… Bernd Greifeneder, Founder and CTO at Dynatrace
summary: Bernd Greifeneder, Founder and CTO of Dynatrace, discusses the biggest challenges for his clients, which involve transforming into software businesses and moving towards an Autonomous Cloud with automated operations. He expresses excitement about deterministic AI and its application in complex IT environments, highlighting Dynatrace's successful reinvention from application performance management to software intelligence. Greifeneder also shares his greatest success, Dynatrace's IPO, and a lesson learned from a past failure in market analysis.

title: New CEO at Ebay, Microsoft launches its e-commerce tool and international transit time to be reduced in Brazil. E-commerce news by Nabil.
summary: This article covers major e-commerce news including Devin Wenig stepping down as eBay CEO, Microsoft launching its Dynamics 365 Commerce tool to compete in the e-commerce solutions market, and Brazil's national Correios significantly reducing international transit times. It also highlights Rent the Runway's supply chain issues, JD.com's efforts to speed up deliveries, and advancements in drone delivery by FedEx, Walgreens, and Wing Aviation. Additionally, the article notes the U.S. remaining in the Universal Postal Union and Narvar's partnership with Walgreens for Urban Outfitters' pick-up services.

title: Motorola, known for cellphones, is fast becoming a major player in government surveillance and artificial intelligence
summary: Motorola Solutions, the successor to the mobile phone business, is investing heavily in government surveillance and artificial intelligence technologies. The company has spent $1.7 billion since 2017 to acquire or support companies specializing in police body cameras, facial recognition, video analytics, and automated license plate readers. This consolidation of surveillance tools under one corporation raises significant privacy concerns about the government's increasing ability to monitor individuals.

title: Why Did Microsoft’s Stock Fall after LinkedIn Offer?
summary: Microsoft's stock fell 2.6% after its announcement to acquire LinkedIn for $26.2 billion, while LinkedIn's stock rose significantly. This market reaction is attributed to Microsoft's historical track record of unsuccessful large acquisitions, leading to investor skepticism regarding the LinkedIn deal. The article points to past acquisitions like aQuantive and Nokia's mobile division, which resulted in substantial write-downs for Microsoft.

title: Want a Really Hard Machine Learning Problem? Try Agriculture, Says John Deere Labs
summary: John Deere Labs posits that agriculture presents the world's most challenging machine learning problems, surpassing autonomous vehicles or cancer detection. The complexity stems from immense data variability in real-world farming conditions, such as diverse crop types, changing grounds, and "dirty data" from various sources. The company is actively recruiting software engineers to tackle these difficult problems, emphasizing that their work matters for feeding a growing population.

title: Between a Wi-Fi rock and a high-tech place: Expedia preaches connectivity and productivity in new Seattle HQ
summary: Expedia is moving its 4,500 employees into a new 40-acre waterfront campus in Seattle, designed for hyperconnectivity and collaboration. The new office space, a $900 million project, emphasizes an open floor plan, universal desks, and 100% Wi-Fi coverage from 1,200 access points, including hidden ones in fake rocks. An "EG Navigator" app helps employees find their way around the massive campus and locate co-workers, reflecting Expedia's focus on productivity and a consistent global workspace experience.

title: Interface CEO Jay Gould on optimism, talking to boards and truly carbon-negative products
summary: Jay Gould, CEO of Interface, discusses the company's ambitious Climate Take Back mission, aiming for truly carbon-negative products and operations. He emphasizes the importance of changing manufacturing processes, educating employees, and advocating for a focus on embodied carbon in construction, while expressing optimism about human ingenuity and the growing positivity around climate action. Gould also highlights Interface's belief that purpose and profit are symbiotic and advocates for corporate governance reform to address climate change.

title: What’s Changed: the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Access Management
summary: Gartner's 2019 Magic Quadrant for Access Management highlights the increasing importance of SaaS delivery, UEBA, and MFA in access management solutions. The report evaluates 14 providers, noting significant movements among visionaries and leaders while identifying key trends and capabilities expected to shape the AM market in the coming years.

title: Xbox corporate vice president Mike Ybarra announces departure from Microsoft
summary: Mike Ybarra, Corporate Vice President of Microsoft's gaming division (Xbox and PC), announced his departure from the company after nearly 20 years. Ybarra oversaw key Xbox services like Xbox Live, Game Pass, and Mixer, and expressed his excitement for a "next adventure." Head of Xbox Phil Spencer thanked Ybarra for his significant contributions and advocacy for gamers.

title: Adobe shuts down service to Venezuela
summary: Adobe has ceased operations in Venezuela to comply with a US executive order banning trade between the two countries, requiring users to save their documents by October 28. This move has sparked debate over the subscription model for software and raised concerns among human rights advocates about its impact on NGOs and independent media. While Adobe monitors the situation, other major tech companies like Google, PayPal, and Microsoft have not yet followed suit.

title: eBay Powers Up First-Ever Gaming Weekend, the Ultimate 72-hour Celebration of Gamer-Favorite Consoles, Releases, Accessories, eSports Gear and More
summary: eBay is launching its first-ever Gaming Weekend from October 11-13, offering deals on consoles, games, and accessories from top brands. The 72-hour event will feature discounts, special releases, and opportunities for shoppers to sell their gear. Highlights include savings on Nintendo, HyperX, and other major gaming brands, along with "Friday Drops" for coveted new items.

title: Xbox corporate vice president Mike Ybarra is leaving Microsoft
summary: Mike Ybarra, Xbox corporate vice president and a recognizable face at Xbox, is departing Microsoft after 20 years. He announced his departure on Twitter, indicating he will remain in the gaming industry and aims to "make gaming better for everyone." Phil Spencer and other Xbox employees expressed their support and thanked Ybarra for his contributions.

title: Construction teams for Microsoft's new corporate campus outside Seattle use drones to update 100 BIM models in real-time
summary: Microsoft's new corporate campus in Redmond, Washington, is utilizing advanced digital technology tools for its construction, including autonomous drones for real-time updates. These drones perform weekly GPS scans to feed over 100 Building Information Models (BIM) containing nearly three million 3D components. This data-driven approach provides "quantifiable accountability" to better manage the project, evaluate pay applications, and predict schedules.

title: Semiconductor stocks are poised to benefit as industry sales growth resumes in 2020
summary: Semiconductor stocks are expected to see a rebound in sales growth in 2020, following a "reset" year in 2019. Despite volatility, these stocks have historically been strong long-term investments. The industry, significantly impacted by U.S.-China trade tensions, anticipates a return to growth with companies like Nvidia projected to see a 17% sales increase next year.

title: The deal that ignited Utah’s tech explosion
summary: The 2009 acquisition of Orem-based web analytics company Omniture by Adobe for $1.8 billion is identified as a pivotal moment that ignited Utah's tech explosion. This deal helped fuel the growth of Utah's homegrown tech sector, leading to significant job creation and wage growth in the state. The article also discusses Adobe's subsequent expansion and the broader impact on the "Silicon Slopes" phenomenon, comparing it to later acquisitions like SAP's purchase of Qualtrics.

title: How Amazon.com moved into the business of U.S. elections
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has significantly expanded its presence in the U.S. election technology sector since 2016, with over 40 states using its services for various election-related functions and both major political parties relying on its cloud. While offering secure and cost-effective solutions for election administrators, this centralization raises concerns among security experts about potential vulnerabilities and the impact of a single major breach. Amazon maintains its systems are reliable and faults in past data exposures were due to customer errors, even as it continues to face scrutiny over its growing influence.

title: Waiting for the Quantum Simulation Revolution
summary: Quantum computers, while promising for chemistry, drug development, and materials science, still require substantial development to compete with conventional computers. Despite making progress in simulating molecules like water, current quantum machines are far from matching the accuracy and scale of classical simulation methods. Experts acknowledge the challenges but anticipate initial impacts in areas where classical simulations struggle, particularly through hybrid systems combining quantum and classical approaches.

title: Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2020
summary: Gartner has identified the top 10 strategic technology trends for 2020, emphasizing a "people-centric smart spaces" approach. These trends include technologies like hyperautomation, multiexperience, human augmentation, and practical blockchain, all aimed at delivering disruptive potential and rapid growth. The report highlights how these technologies will impact customers, employees, and society, creating more immersive and intelligent experiences.

title: NVIDIA with Microsoft Announces Technology Collaboration for Era of Intelligent Edge
summary: NVIDIA and Microsoft have announced a technology collaboration focused on intelligent edge computing to help industries manage and gain insights from vast amounts of data. This partnership integrates Microsoft Azure with the NVIDIA EGX platform and NVIDIA T4 GPUs to accelerate AI capabilities from the edge to the cloud. The collaboration aims to enable breakthrough experiences for customers across various industries, including retail, manufacturing, and smart cities.

title: CRM Watchlist Winners 2019: Once Again, Pegasystems
summary: Pegasystems won the CRM Watchlist 2019 for its strong narrative, product offerings, and overall market impact. The article details Pegasystems' evolution from BPM to customer engagement, highlighting its Pega Infinity platform, its "Empathetic AI" initiative, and suggesting areas for continued impact such as e-commerce integration, refining its vision, and enhancing thought leadership.

title: Harvest sign as new Microsoft Innovation Centre partners
summary: Harvest Technology has signed an agreement with Microsoft Malta to become the first new partner of the Microsoft Innovation Centre (MIC). This partnership aims to leverage Harvest's expertise and market presence to support the local startup ecosystem. The MIC, which has been growing in Malta, plans to announce more such partnerships to further empower individuals and organizations through Microsoft's technology.

title: F5 Networks and Amazon Web Services team up in cloud partnership of Seattle tech giants
summary: F5 Networks and Amazon Web Services have formed a multi-year cloud partnership, bringing together their sales teams and paving the way for future technology integrations. This alliance aims to simplify the creation of cloud-native applications using F5 on AWS and facilitate the migration of existing applications to the cloud. The announcement coincided with F5's strong Q4 2019 financial results, beating Wall Street expectations, despite the ongoing transition from hardware to software and the integration of NGINX.

title: Microsoft gaming revenue down 7% YoY
summary: Microsoft's gaming revenue decreased by 7% year-over-year in the first fiscal quarter of 2020 (July-September 2019), totaling $2.54 billion, which is $196 million less than the previous year. This decline is largely attributed to a 34% drop in console sales, although revenues from content and services remained flat and Xbox software and services revenue saw a 1% increase.

title: Workday: Procurement Rising? 5 Scenarios Explored
summary: This article examines Workday's growing focus on procurement as a key driver for future growth, especially following its acquisition of Scout RFP. It explores five potential scenarios for Workday's procurement product development, ranging from a basic extension of financials to a comprehensive approach leveraging its HCM strengths. The analysis raises questions about Workday's ability to compete effectively in the source-to-pay market and advises customers to evaluate current offerings rather than relying solely on roadmaps.

title: Fertility benefits company Progyny starts strong after IPO
summary: Progyny, a Manhattan fertility benefits management company, saw its shares surge on its first day of trading on Nasdaq after an IPO that raised about $82 million. The company aims to address limited fertility benefits offered by employers and considers its profitability and public listing a way to elevate its stature in the industry. Progyny covers 1.4 million members across approximately 80 employers and reported $4 million in net income and $103.4 million in revenue in the first six months of the year.

title: Texas to provide Microsoft $4.9M grant as part of Las Colinas workforce expansion
summary: Texas has awarded Microsoft Corporation a nearly $4.9 million grant to support the company's expansion in Las Colinas, which includes a $31 million investment and the creation of 575 new jobs. The grant comes from the Texas Enterprise Fund and highlights Microsoft's commitment to the area, affirming Texas' status as a technology hub.

title: HP Takes Printers Into the Cloud With Workpath, Command Center
summary: HP Inc. is introducing HP Workpath and HP Command Center to bring its multifunction printers into the cloud era, offering new revenue streams and customer loyalty opportunities for channel partners. Workpath enables app development for printers to simplify business processes, while Command Center provides cloud-based management and enhanced security for MFPs. These innovations aim to reduce labor for IT, improve security posture, and create new service offerings for partners like ImageNet Consulting.

title: Dell’s Israel R&D Head Promoted to Global Head of Storage
summary: Dan Inbar, Dell EMC’s vice president and general manager of its Israeli R&D centers, has been promoted to global head of storage while retaining his current role. The Israeli R&D branch, established in 2006, employs over 1200 people focusing on various advanced technologies. Dell EMC has a history of acquiring and investing in Israeli startups, with over $1 billion spent on acquisitions and investments through its Dell Technologies Capital arm.

title: Gartner names Microsoft a Leader in the 2019 Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) Magic Quadrant
summary: Gartner has named Microsoft a Leader in its 2019 Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) Magic Quadrant, recognizing its completeness of vision and ability to execute. Microsoft attributes this recognition to its commitment to building a top-tier CASB solution, Microsoft Cloud App Security, which offers extensive integration and advanced threat protection. The company emphasizes its strong vision for a customer-centric solution that seamlessly integrates with existing environments.

title: Cisco alums reunite: Prem Jain’s Pensando spins into the edge-computing conversation
summary: Pensando Systems Inc., led by former Cisco executives including Prem Jain and John Chambers, has emerged from stealth mode with an ambitious plan to transform edge computing. The company aims to compete with Amazon Web Services Inc.'s Nitro by bringing critical IT services to the edge using programmable chips, replacing numerous appliances and simplifying architectures. Pensando’s technology leverages a "flow-based" approach, which they believe offers a distinct advantage in the industry.

title: Introducing the Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG)
summary: The Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) began trading on NASDAQ on October 29, 2019, seeking to invest in companies benefiting from increased cybersecurity technology adoption. The article details the growing threat of cybercrime, driven by the explosion of data and digital technologies like IoT and cloud computing, emphasizing its financial and societal costs. It highlights the increasing global spending on cybersecurity by individuals, companies, and governments as a critical measure against evolving cyberthreats.

title: At Domino’s Biggest Franchisee, a Chatbot Named “Dottie” Speeds Up Hiring
summary: RPM Pizza, the largest Domino's franchisee in the U.S., has significantly sped up its hiring process for hourly workers by implementing a text message-based chatbot named "Dottie." The chatbot, which handles initial screening and interview scheduling, reduced hiring time from up to five days to between one and three, helping the company secure candidates faster in a competitive job market. This innovation has also contributed to a substantial decrease in RPM's yearly employee turnover.

title: PTC’s Onshape Acquisition: Did SOLIDWORKS Founder Jon Hirschtick Have to Sell?
summary: PTC acquired Jon Hirschtick's cloud CAD company Onshape for $470 million, marking Hirschtick's second major CAD company sale. The article explores whether Onshape *had* to sell due to financial pressures, given its 5,000 paying users falling short of its 10,000 break-even target, or if the sale was a strategic move to leverage PTC's market presence and resources for accelerated growth in the evolving SaaS CAD market. It also discusses the strategic rationale behind PTC's acquisition, driven by CEO Jim Heppelmann's vision for SaaS, cloud-based solutions, and his previous successful bets on IoT and AR/VR.

title: Ex-SAP CEO Bill McDermott Named New ServiceNow CEO
summary: Former SAP CEO Bill McDermott has been appointed as the new CEO and President of ServiceNow, replacing John Donahoe who is moving to Nike. This announcement comes shortly after McDermott's departure from SAP, where he led a significant shift to cloud computing. Following the news, ServiceNow's shares experienced a drop, despite reporting strong third-quarter results and maintaining robust full-year guidance.

title: Progyny finds fertile ground in fertility-benefits field
summary: Progyny, a fertility benefits company, has seen early success on Nasdaq and is a rapidly growing company in the women's health tech field. The company manages fertility benefits for 1.4 million employees, including those at Google and Microsoft, and boasts a higher success rate for helping women conceive compared to the national average. Despite competition from other women's health companies and traditional insurers, Progyny differentiates itself through patient outcomes and cost savings for employers.

title: What Has Been Driving Akamai Technologies’ Performance?
summary: Akamai Technologies (NASDAQ: AKAM) exceeded Q3 revenue and EPS expectations, primarily driven by strong growth in its security solutions business. This positive performance led to an upward revision of the company's guidance for Q4 and full-year 2019. The article highlights Akamai's shift from its core content delivery network (CDN) business, which faces competition from large internet players, towards leveraging its network reliability and insights to build a robust security business and become a key player in edge computing.

summary: Microsoft and Salesforce are expanding their strategic partnership to enhance customer success, with Salesforce naming Microsoft Azure as its public cloud provider for Salesforce Marketing Cloud. summary: Finnish telecoms company Elisa is expanding its industrial IoT monitoring and insights solution to 100 Procter & Gamble factories, building on an initial rollout at 10 sites. summary: Logitech G has introduced the Adaptive Gaming Kit, a collection of buttons and triggers compatible with Microsoft's Xbox Adaptive Controller, designed for gamers with accessibility needs. This kit provides a range of configurable controls at a more affordable price point, developed in collaboration with Microsoft Inclusive Tech Lab and leading accessibility groups. Logitech G aims to promote inclusivity and diversity in gaming, enabling more individuals to experience the joys of play through this new product.

summary: IBM and Bank of America are collaborating to develop the world's first financial services-ready public cloud, designed to meet the highly regulated needs of the banking industry. summary: The U.S. Justice Department is moving to terminate a 70-year-old antitrust settlement that prevented Hollywood studios from owning movie theaters and dictating which films they would show. This move, stemming from the 1948 Paramount Pictures consent decrees, is aimed at fostering "consumer-friendly innovation" as new entertainment services like Netflix have made the old rules irrelevant. While cinema chains' stocks rose on the news, some analysts are skeptical about major studios buying theater chains given the shift towards streaming.
